L2020: ## Anti-Raxibacumab Antibodies
L2021: Fifteen of 18 rabbits (83%) in the levofloxacin/raxibacumab group tested positive for anti-raxibacumab antibodies on Day 28. Six of 19 (31.6%) rabbits in the levofloxacin group also tested positive for anti-raxibacumab antibodies on Day 28 although the levofloxacin only treatment group did not receive raxibacumab. The Applicant suggested the anti-PA response may have included antibodies that cross-reacted in the anti-human anti-PA assay, and given the modest incidence of anti-raxibacumab immunogenicity at low titers compared with the raxibacumab-treated animals, this explanation is plausible. The emergence of potential anti-raxibacumab immunogenicity did not negatively impact survival.
L2022: ## 6.1.7 Subpopulations
L2023: The three treatment groups each consisted of 50% male and 50% female rabbits. Given the small numbers of animals, subpopulation analysis according to sex was not performed.
L2024: ## 6.1.8 Analysis of Clinical Information Relevant to Dosing Recommendations
L2025: N/A
L2026: ## 6.1.9 Discussion of Persistence of Efficacy and/or Tolerance Effects
L2027: As discussed previously, anti-PA and TNA assays were conducted on surviving animals only. All animals with the exception of one (K99234 in the levofloxacin group) were anti-PA antibody negative at baseline, and all tested positive for anti-PA antibodies at Day
L2028: 28. All animals in the active treatment groups were TNA negative at baseline and tested positive for TNA at Day 28, with the exception of 1 survivor in the levofloxacin/raxibacumab group (K99224) which tested negative for TNA at baseline and at Day 28. This animal did not test positive for PA toxemia or bacteremia during the study but was positive for anti-PA antibodies at Day 28.
L2029: While surviving animals were not challenged with a second anthrax exposure after recovering from the initial exposure to test the persistence of efficacy, the presence of anti-PA antibody at 28 days suggests that protective efficacy should theoretically be present at 28 days and for the duration the antibody persists. However no formal studies have assessed the longevity or functionality of anti-PA antibody at defined time points after the initial exposure.
L2030: No studies on tolerance have been conducted.
L2031: ## 6.1.10 Additional Efficacy Issues/Analyses
L2032: ## Summary of Study 789-G923702
L2033: Evaluation of the Efficacy of Raxibacumab in Combination with Ciprofloxacin for Therapeutic Treatment in the Cynomolgus Monkey Inhalation Anthrax Model
L2034: Please see the complete review by Dr. Susan McCune in the Appendix of this review. A brief summary follows:
L2035: This was a parallel-group, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled GLP study in 40 healthy male and female cynomolgus monkeys to evaluate the efficacy of raxibacumab in combination with ciprofloxacin as a therapeutic treatment in cynomolgus monkeys with inhalation anthrax
L2036: ## Efficacy conclusions:
L2037: - Both the ciprofloxacin treated group and the ciprofloxacin/raxibacumab treated group showed statistically significant superiority over placebo in both the sponsor's ITT analysis and the FDA primary analysis.
- For the FDA primary analysis, the survival rate in the placebo group was 0%, the survival rate in the ciprofloxacin treated group was 100% and the survival rate in the ciprofloxacin/raxibacumab treated group was 84.6%. The treated groups were superior to placebo (p&lt;0.0001).
- There were no differences in survival rates between the two treated groups.
L2038: ## Safety conclusions:
L2039: - Safety data were limited in the study to findings on gross necropsy, histopathology, and serial CBCs.
L2040: - In the placebo animals, 11 animals had evidence of low CNS pathology while 1 animal had high CNS pathology. That animal inadvertently was exposed to ciprofloxacin. Only one treated animal died of anthrax disease and that animal had evidence of hemorrhagic meningitis that affected the entire brain. No surviving animals were sacrificed.
- Based on the available analyses, the pathophysiologic basis for the increased CNS inflammation seen in the pivotal efficacy trial in cynomolgus monkeys is not clear. The number of animals analyzed is small. While it is reassuring that no gross neurologic findings were seen in the surviving animals, and no brain abnormalities were seen in toxicologic studies, a potential interaction between anthrax and raxibacumab contributing to CNS inflammation and hemorrhage cannot be ruled out. It will be important to examine the histopathology in animals that die in any subsequent studies and it would be reassuring to examine the brains of those animals that survive in order to establish normal brain histology in survivors. If it is not possible to sacrifice survivors, then more formal neurologic assessments including imaging studies should be performed in subsequent studies.
L2041: ## 7 Review of Safety
L2042: ## Safety Summary
L2043: The safety database consisted of 326 healthy subjects treated with the recommended dose of raxibacumab of 40 mg/kg manufactured by the M11 process (the version intended for licensure), with 303 subjects receiving a single dose (studies HGS1021-C1064 and HGS1021-C1063), 23 subjects receiving a 2nd dose 2 weeks after their first dose (study HGS1021-1063), and 20 subjects from study HGS1021-C1064 who received a 2nd dose more than 4 months after their initial dose (study HGS1021-C1069). In Study HGS1021-C1064, 48 subjects who received raxibacumab also received ciprofloxacin as part of this drug interaction study.
L2044: The M11 formulation of raxibacumab is safe for use in the adult population at the intended single IV dose of 40 mg/kg when administered after diphenhydramine pre-medication. There was only 1 death in a placebo-treated subject from injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident which was not related to raxibacumab. In addition to this death, there were 2 additional SAEs reported, 1 case of cholecystitis and 1 case of schizophrenia, both of which were likely related to underlying conditions. There were 4 subjects (1.2%) who discontinued raxibacumab during infusion because of AEs. Two of these were cases of urticaria in subjects who did not receive premedication with diphenhydramine. AEs of severe intensity were infrequently reported (1.9%). The most frequently reported AE was headache; other commonly reported AEs included upper respiratory tract infection and rash.
L2045: As the safety database consisted of healthy volunteers, a study agent/disease interaction could not be directly assessed. While CNS AEs were reviewed, it appears from the animal models that systemic anthrax disease must be present for CNS pathology to be observed. A review for CNS safety in humans was therefore limited. Other limitations with respect to safety include the exclusion of pediatric subjects and pregnant patients from the safety database. While subjects greater than 65 years of age were enrolled in the study, they represented only 6.4%(21/326) of the population which is insufficient to make any conclusions as to whether these subjects respond differently to raxibacumab compared to subjects less than 65 years of age. Similarly, non-white subjects represented 28% of the safety database. Therefore, it is unclear how generalizable the results of raxibacumab safety assessments are to the above populations.
L2046: ## 7.1 Methods
L2047: A review of the integrated summary of safety (ISS) database was performed for this BLA. The safety data on raxibacumab product manufactured using the M10 manufacturing process was not included in this analysis; only safety studies that used raxibacumab manufactured by the M11 process intended for licensure, were considered.
L2048: Therefore the safety database consists of 326 subjects treated with the recommended dose of raxibacumab of 40 mg/kg manufactured by the M11 process, with 303 subjects receiving a single dose (studies HGS1021-C1064 and HGS1021-C1063), 23 subjects receiving a 2nd dose 2 weeks after their first dose (study HGS1021-1063), and 20 subjects from study HGS1021-C1064 who received a 2nd dose more than 4 months after their initial dose (study HGS1021-C1069).

L2055: ## 7.1.2 Categorization of Adverse Events
L2056: Usual definitions were used in the definition and categorization of adverse events.
L2057: An adverse event was defined as any unfavorable or unintended sign, symptom, or disease that is temporally associated with the use of a study agent but is not necessarily caused by the study agent. This included worsening (e.g., increase in frequency or severity) of pre-existing conditions. All AEs that were identified from the start of study agent administration on Day 0 through Day 56 (single-dose subjects) or Day 70 (double-dose subjects) were to be recorded on the AE CRF. The record of each AE on the CRF included AE description or diagnosis, start date, end date, whether the AE was ongoing, seriousness, severity, action taken with study agent, relationship to study agent (causality), and outcome. It was required that all data fields on the AE CRF be completed.
L2058: The severity of an AE was graded using the modified DMID toxicity tables. For AEs not included in these toxicity tables, the following guidelines applied:
L2059: - Mild - causing no limitation of usual activities
- Moderate - causing some limitation of usual activities
- Severe - causing inability to carry out usual activities
- Life-threatening - potentially life threatening or disabling
L2060: A serious adverse event was defined as any AE resulting in any of the following outcomes:
L2061: - Death
- Was life threatening (i.e., was an immediate threat to life)
- Inpatient hospitalization
- Prolongation of an existing hospitalization
- Persistent or significant disability or incapacity
- Congenital anomaly or birth defect
- Medically important
L2062: The causality assessment was to be made by the investigator based on information available at the time that the SAE worksheet was completed.
L2063: ## 7.1.3 Pooling of Data Across Studies/Clinical Trials to Estimate and Compare Incidence
L2064: All single dose exposures were pooled for analysis. This included subjects from studies HGS1021-C1064 and HGS1021-C1063. Double dose subjects were presented both separately (study HGS1021-1063, where subjects received a second dose 2 weeks after their initial dose, and study HGS1021-C1069, where subjects received a second dose more than 4 months after their initial dose) and pooled for analysis.
L2065: ## 7.2 Adequacy of Safety Assessments
L2066: ## 7.2.1 Overall Exposure at Appropriate Doses/Durations and Demographics of Target Populations
L2067: Subjects enrolled in the 3 analyzed safety studies all received a single target therapeutic dose of raxibacumab 40 mg/kg IV. Forty-six additional subjects received a second 40 mg/kg IV dose to investigate the immunogenicity of the product.
L2068: In study HGS1021-C1064, 5 of the first 25 subjects (20%) dosed with raxibacumab developed dermatologic events following IV raxibacumab administration. Three subjects responded to oral diphenhydramine, and 2 had discontinuation of their treatment with resolution of the event (1 with diphenhydramine, 1 spontaneous). Following these observations, the protocol was amended (9 May 2007) to specify administration of diphenhydramine 50 mg PO prior to dosing with raxibacumab. At the completion of HGS1021-C1064, rash was reported in 8 subjects (9.1%, 8/88). The incidence of rash among subjects who did not receive diphenhydramine was 6/27 (22.2%), while the incidence of rash among subjects who received diphenhydramine was 2/61 (3.3%). All subjects enrolled in the subsequent Studies HGS1021-C1063 and HGS1021-C1069 received diphenhydramine prior to raxibacumab infusion. In Study HGS1021-C1063, the rate of rash (preferred terms rash and urticaria) was 2.5% in both placebo and raxibacumab-treated subjects.

L2077: ## 7.2.2 Explorations for Dose Response
L2078: One dose escalation study was performed in the raxibacumab development program. Study PAM-NH-01, which used the M10 formulation of the product, was a phase 1 single-blind, placebo-controlled, single-injection study which evaluated the safety and pharmacokinetics of 3 different single doses of PA mAb [0.3 mg/kg, 1 mg/kg and 3 mg/kg given intramuscularly (IM in 2 different sites – gluteus and vastus lateralis)] and 5 different single doses of PA mAb [1 mg/kg, 3 mg/kg, 10 mg/kg, 20 mg/kg and 40 mg/kg given intravenously (IV)] in healthy subjects. While this first in man study predominantly used doses well below the putative therapeutic dose and assessed the safety of a developmental product rather than the to-be-marketed scale-up product, it did not find any dose-related AEs. Dose response exploration for the M11 formulation was limited only to subjects who received 2 doses of raxibacumab 14 days apart (Study HGS1021-C1063), but would not include subjects enrolled in Study HGS1021-1069 who received
L2079: their second dose more than 4 months after the first dose, as washout was complete by this time.

L2086: The number of subjects reporting at least 1 AE was higher in the single dose group (50.5%) compared to either of the two double-dose groups prior to their 2nd dose (17.4% and 30%). This observation may be related to the small study numbers in the double dose groups. The number of subjects reporting at least 1 AE post 2nd dose was also lower (approximately 40% in both groups), which again could be related to small study numbers, or the absence of a dose-adverse event relationship when a second raxibacumab dose is administered 2 weeks or later following the first dose. Overall, the numbers of SAEs and AEs of severe intensity were infrequently reported.
L2087: ## 7.2.3 Special Animal and/or In Vitro Testing
L2088: Three relevant nonclinical studies were reviewed in detail by the Pharmacology/Toxicology team and are briefly summarized here:
L2089: The initial ex vivo tissue cross-reactivity study in human and cynomolgus monkey tissue showed specific cytoplasmic (non-membrane) binding of raxibacumab (M10 manufacturing process) in skeletal muscle and thyroid (both species), endometrium (human only) and breast and prostate (monkey only). These tissues were identified as possible target organs for toxicity.
L2090: The second ex vivo tissue cross-reactivity study was performed on tissues of NZW rabbit, cynomolgus macaque, and man and tested raxibacumab from to-be-licensed M11 manufacturing process. This study showed no thyroid histopathology or abnormal levels of circulating thyroid hormones. Please refer to Dr. Terry Miller's summary in Section 4.3 Preclinical Pharmacology/Toxicology for additional information on these studies.
L2091: Regarding safety, three non-clinical studies were reviewed in detail for the purposes of the CDC IND and are briefly summarized here:
L2092: The 120-day monkey study evaluated raxibacumab 40 mg/kg given on days 0, 13, and 25, either IM or IV and again at day 69 by IM route. No difference in weight or feeding between the placebo and raxibacumab arms, and no gross pathological changes in the study arms were reported. Local inflammation resulting from trauma at site of IM injection was noted. Some animals had microcysts in the thyroid. Some animals had chronic inflammation in the prostate. These findings were consistent with the tissue cross-reactivity study above. CPK and thyroid hormones were reported to be unremarkable. Although the histological findings were not judged to be significant, these organs were mentioned as possible targets of toxicity. No anti Fab or Fc antibodies were found in these animals. There were no gross or histopathological CNS changes reported.
L2093: The rabbit embryo-fetal toxicity study tested raxibacumab 0, 40, 120 mg/kg IV on gestation days 7 and 14. No adverse effects on the fetus or mother were identified, and the NOAEL was determined to be 120 mg/kg, the highest dose tested. Minor skeletal variations were noted, but these were not considered as adverse effects, and were stated to be within the rate for such variations seen in rabbits. It was briefly noted that in this study, 4 animals (2/20 in 40 mg/kg arm, 2/20 in 120 mg/kg arm) with anti-raxibacumab antibodies had reduced serum raxibacumab levels compared to animals without such antibodies. However, caution should be exercised when interpreting the significance of these findings, as detection of the anti-raxibacumab antibodies is hindered when the raxibacumab concentration exceeds 150 mcg/mL.

L2100: ## 7.3 Major Safety Results
L2101: ## 7.3.1 Deaths
L2102: There was only 1 death reported among the 326 subjects. Subject US001-002 was enrolled in study HGS1021-C1063 and randomized to the placebo double-dose group. This subject died from injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident. A narrative of the event follows:
L2103: Subject US001-002, was a 45-year-old white female in the placebo double-dose group, and she received the infusions of study drug per protocol on Day 0 and Day 14. No relevant medical history or concomitant medications were reported. The subject was involved in a motorcycle accident that occurred 25 days after the 2nd placebo dose (Day 39), and died as a result of injuries sustained in the accident. The investigator indicated that the injuries sustained in the accident (life-threatening) were not related to study agent.

L2110: The narratives for the remaining SAES are provided below:
L2111: ## **Subject US001-017**
L2112: Subject US001-017, a 52-year-old white female in the raxibacumab double-dose group, developed upper abdominal pain, nausea, and low grade fever 10 days after her 2nd raxibacumab dose (Day 24). The subject was hospitalized and underwent a cholecystectomy on Day 26; the post-operative diagnosis was confirmed to be cholecystitis. Dosing was completed and no action was taken with regard to raxibacumab. The investigator indicated that the cholecystitis (severe) was possibly related to raxibacumab, and most likely caused by progression of concurrent disease as the subject had multiple risk factors for cholelithiasis including female gender, age, obesity (body weight of 111.5 kg), elevated serum glucose and elevated triglycerides.
L2113: ## **Subject US001-005**
L2114: A 48-year-old black male received his 1st dose of ciprofloxacin (500 mg PO) on Day 0 (31Jan 2007) and his raxibacumab dose (40 mg/kgIV) on Day 5 per protocol. Relevant medical history which was not disclosed at screening included diagnoses of schizophrenia, depression, and bipolar disorder. There were no concomitant medications taken. The subject completed ciprofloxacin dosing as planned on Day 7. At the Day 47 follow-up visit, the subject reported auditory hallucinations occurring 2 to 3 times per week. He stated that the auditory hallucinations began after receiving raxibacumab; however, he did not report this to the clinical staff at that time. The subject denied suicidal ideation. The subject denied prior history of symptoms before entering the study and denied any history of psychiatric illness for himself or his family. A physical examination was within normal limits with no evidence of agitation, anxiety or depression. The subject left the clinical unit prior to completing further psychiatric evaluation. The subject later returned for evaluation and disclosed a past medical history of depression, bipolar disorder, and schizophrenia dating back to his early 20s. On Day 61, the subject was diagnosed with schizophrenia and prescribed olanzapine. As the subject received all 15 ciprofloxacin doses and the single raxibacumab dose per study schedule prior to disclosing the SAE, no action was taken with regard to study agents. The investigator revised the event term to schizophrenia with a severity grading of life-threatening, and indicated that it was probably not related to raxibacumab or ciprofloxacin. The schizophrenia was ongoing at the end of the study.
L2115: *MO comment: The SAEs of cholecystitis and schizophrenia are unlikely to be due to raxibacumab based on temporal presentation and the presence of pre-existing conditions which could account for the SAEs.*

The clonus led to discontinuation of the raxibacumab infusion, and both AEs resolved in 1 day.
L2124: There were 2 subjects enrolled in Study HGS1021-C1063 who had treatment discontinuation. Subject US002-011 was randomized to a single dose of raxibacumab, and described the event “difficulty breathing” of moderate severity and non-serious during infusion and only received a partial dose. There were no other associated AEs of anaphylaxis or rash, and no changes in vital signs. The subject recovered within 20 minutes of discontinuation of the drug. The investigator attributed the subject’s symptoms as most likely due to esophageal spasm caused by rapid eating prior to the infusion and/or anxiousness. This subject completed follow-up. Subject US001-022 had the AE of moderate skin infection on his left hand on Day 12 which was not related to raxibacumab and resolved. This subject did not receive his second placebo dose but completed follow-up.
L2125: *MO comment: Urticaria was likely related to raxibacumab, as neither subject received premedication with diphenhydramine as recommended.*
L2126: *With respect to the clonic muscular contractions and facial flushing in Subject US003-028, one condition which would relate the two AEs is serotonin syndrome. Typically symptom onset is rapid, with a triad of abnormalities seen: Cognitive effects (headache, agitation), autonomic effects (tachycardia, diaphoresis, hypertension, hyperthermia) and somatic effects (clonus, tremor). The subject’s vital signs were unchanged 30 minutes post-dose and no other symptoms were recorded. Although her symptoms resolved upon discontinuation of raxibacumab without additional intervention suggesting a possible relationship to raxibacumab, the investigator also noted anxiety could account for these symptoms.*
L2127: *The AE of dyspnea was unlikely related to raxibacumab as per the investigator’s assessment.*

L2134: ## Influenza
L2135: Subject US004-000030 was a 22 year old white male enrolled in Study HGS-1021-C1063 randomized to the single dose raxibacumab arm. The subject had the following AEs recorded: rhinitis (study day 7), clavicle fracture (study day 25), influenza (study day 36), headache (study day 36), vomiting and pyrexia (study day 41). All were non-serious (all coded as mild except clavicle fracture which was moderate and influenza which was severe), no action was taken for any of the AEs and all resolved at the end of study except for the clavicle fracture. Given the delayed onset of influenza, it is unlikely to be related to study drug.
L2136: ## Blood amylase increased
L2137: Subject US003-00002 was a 54 year old white male enrolled in Study HGS-1021-C1063 randomized to the single dose raxibacumab arm. His screening amylase was elevated at 159 U/L (range 28-100 U/L) but was normal on days 0 and 1. On study day 14, it was elevated again at 208 U/L, but was normal again by study day 28. The subject had several readings of elevated glucose throughout the study. No action was taken for the elevated amylase level.
L2138: *MO comment: Given the episodic elevations in amylase prior to enrollment in the study and after discharge, it is possible that the subject had chronic pancreatitis. While this could have been due to raxibacumab, the elevated level at screening and again at day 14 suggests a different etiology.*
L2139: ## Blood creatine phosphokinase increased
L2140: Subject US003-000042 was a 22 year old black male enrolled in Study HGS-1021-C1064 randomized to the IV Cipro/IV Raxibacumab/PO Cipro arm. On study day 42, the subject had elevated blood creatine phosphokinase (5206 U/L, normal 24-204 U/L), as well as elevated AST (91 IU/L, normal 0-40 IU/L) although the ALT, ALP and GGT were normal (45 U/L, range 0-55 U/L; 25 IU/L, range 25-150 IU/L; and 12 IU/L, range 0-65 IU/L respectively), as well as amylase, total bilirubin and LDH. The CK elevation was deemed severe while the liver enzyme elevation was coded as mild. These AEs were noted for 15 days, on day 56 the CK was 87 U/L. No action was taken regarding these laboratory findings and the investigator thought these AEs were probably not related to the study drug.
L2141: *MO comment: The Sponsors' Integrated Summary of Safety stated that the CK elevation was temporally related to increased physical activity and not accompanied by any clinical symptoms indicating an acute cardiac event.*
L2142: ## Prothrombin time prolonged
L2143: Subject US003-000001 was a 26 year old white female enrolled in Study HGS-1021-C1063 randomized to the single dose raxibacumab arm. The subject had a normal PT ratio (INR) on study day 0 (1.2, normal 0.9-1.3), but was found to be prolonged on study day 28 at 2.5. All other hematologic parameters were normal. No action was taken and the investigator did not think this was related to the study drug.
L2144: In summary, none of the AEs of severe intensity were likely related to raxibacumab.
L2145: ## 7.3.5 Submission Specific Primary Safety Concerns
L2146: ## Central Nervous System
L2147: Based on the increased CNS findings in raxibacumab-treated animals that died of anthrax in the pivotal efficacy studies, CNS AEs were examined more closely in the human safety database.

L2153: The main CNS finding in non-survivors on necropsy in the animal studies was meningitis, with the pathologic findings of inflammation, hemorrhage and necrosis. There were no CNS infections reported in the SOC "Infections and infestations" across all studies. Symptoms suggestive of meningitis are headache, fever and meningismus. Headache is nonspecific and was reported in similar numbers of placebo and raxibacumab treated subjects (10% and 9.5%, respectively). There were an additional 2 reports of tension headache in the placebo group.
L2154: With respect to subjects reporting any combination of the triad of symptoms suggestive of meningitis, there were no reports of meningismus across studies. There was 1 raxibacumab treated subject (US004-000030) enrolled in study HGS1021-C1063 who reported fever (mild) on day 41 in conjunction with vomiting (mild), both of 1 day duration with no action taken. Similarly, there was 1 placebo subject US005-000046 enrolled in Study HGS1021-C1063 with pyrexia and headache reported on Study day 36, again of 1 day's duration with no intervention. It is unlikely that either of these represented cases of meningitis.
L2155: ## Rash
L2156: In Study HGS1021-C1064, 5 of the first 25 subjects (20%) enrolled developed Grade 1 to Grade 2 rashes following IV raxibacumab administration which resolved with PO diphenhydramine or without medication. Three subjects responded to oral diphenhydramine, and 2 had discontinuation of their treatment with resolution of the event (1 with diphenhydramine, 1 spontaneous). Following a protocol amendment, subsequent subjects were to be treated with PO diphenhydramine (50 mg) up to 60 minutes prior to the infusion of raxibacumab. Subjects who developed a rash following infusion were to be treated with PO diphenhydramine (25 to 50 mg) Q8h as needed.
L2157: Following this amendment, only 3 additional cases of rash were reported, for a total of 8/88 (9.1%) subjects with mild to moderate infusion related rashes, none of which were above Grade 2 severity. The overall incidence of rash among subjects who did not receive diphenhydramine was 6/27 (22.2%), while the incidence of rash among subjects who received diphenhydramine was 2/61 (3.3%). All subjects enrolled in the subsequent Studies HGS1021-C1063 and HGS1021-C1069 received diphenhydramine prior to raxibacumab infusion. In Study HGS1021-C1063, the rate of rash (preferred terms rash and urticaria) was 2.5% in both placebo and raxibacumab-treated subjects.
L2158: The Applicant attempted to explore the pathophysiology of these infusion related rashes by assessing a panel of immune mediators of allergic response, including histamine, immunoglobulin E levels, eosinophil counts, and a broad panel of cytokines produced by Th1 and/or Th2 cells. There was no consistent pattern indicative of a histamine-mediated allergic response in subjects who experienced rash, nor any pattern suggestive of immune stimulation or an immune complex-mediated process based on the absence of any significant differences in complement levels or cytokine panels.
L2159: The Applicant concluded that the precise etiology or pathophysiology of the observed rashes remained unclear, but argued that the clinical presentation of mild infusion-related rashes with no recurrence suggested an urticarial process associated with localized histamine release. Lastly, they correctly noted that premedication with an antihistamine was able to reduce the incidence of rash.

L2172: ## Central Nervous system
L2173: In the Nervous system disorders SOC, headache was by far the most frequently reported AE and was responsible for the difference in rates observed between the placebo and raxibacumab treated subjects. Headache was reported in 8.8% of single dose subjects, 14% of double dose subjects, and 10% of placebo subjects.
L2174: ## Infections
L2175: In contrast, within the Infections and infestations SOC, upper respiratory tract infection occurred in 11.6% of double dose raxibacumab subjects, compared to 3.9% of single dose raxibacumab subjects and 5.0% of placebo subjects. However, other infections were not reported more frequently in the active treatment groups to suggest a uniform immune effect of raxibacumab. All AEs in the raxibacumab treated subjects ranged in frequency from 0.2% to 4.9%.
L2176: ## Gastrointestinal system
L2177: In the Gastrointestinal disorders SOC, rates of abdominal pain, diarrhea, nausea and vomiting were all higher in the placebo group compared to all raxibacumab subjects.
L2178: ## Skin and subcutaneous tissue system
L2179: In the Skin and subcutaneous tissue disorders SOC, AEs reported by the raxibacumab treated subjects ranged from 0.2% to 2.1% in frequency. Pruritis and rash were reported in all raxibacumab subjects at 2.1% and 1.8% respectively, and were comparable to placebo rates (pruritis 0%, rash 1.3%). As previously mentioned in Section 7.2.1, 5 of 25 subjects (20%) in Study HGS1021-C1064 developed dermatologic events following IV raxibacumab administration. As a result of these findings, the study protocol was amended so that all subsequent subjects received diphenhydramine before raxibacumab infusion. At the completion of HGS1021-C1064, 27 subjects did not receive diphenhydramine, of which 6/27 (22%) developed rash. A total of 8/88 subjects (9.1%) reported rash in the study overall.

L2185: ## Hematology
L2186: Hematologic changes were infrequently reported across studies. The rates of Grade 2 and higher hematology laboratory abnormalities were comparable between placebo-treated subjects and raxibacumab-treated subjects. Among raxibacumab-treated subjects, there was 1 subject each with Grade 3 leukocytosis (Subject US001-069) and Grade 4 neutropenia (Subject US001-029), and 2 subjects with Grade 3 PT (Subjects US006-030, US003-001, and US002-007). All of these were reported in single dose raxibacumab subjects, and each laboratory abnormality resolved on-study.

L2188: ## Hematology Narratives
L2189: ## Leukocytosis
L2190: Subject US001-069 (24 year-old white female in Study HGS1021-C1063, raxibacumab single-dose group) had a Grade 1 (11.44 \times 10^3/\mu\text{L}) white blood cell (WBC) count at baseline, and a transient shift to Grade 3 WBC count (22.17 \times 10^3/\mu\text{L}) on Day 2. This event was recorded as a mild AE (not related, resolved). The subject also had AEs of moderate abdominal pain on Day 3 (not related, resolved), which lasted for 3 days, and mild malaise on Day 4 (possibly related to study agent, resolved), which lasted for 1 day. The investigator indicated that the elevated WBC count was probably not related to raxibacumab and that the most likely cause of the event was a laboratory error.
L2191: ## Neutropenia
L2192: Subject US006-029 (35 year-old white female in Study HGS1021-C1063, raxibacumab single-dose group) had a Grade 0 (4.46 \times 10^3/\mu\text{L}) neutrophil count at baseline, which shifted to Grade 4 (0.41 \times 10^3/\mu\text{L}) on Day 28. This subject's neutrophil count returned to baseline levels (1.7 \times 10^3/\mu\text{L}) by Day 33. This event was recorded as a mild AE (resolved) that was possibly related to study agent.
L2193: ## PT
L2194: Subject US006-030 (41 year-old white male in Study HGS1021-C1063, raxibacumab single-dose group) had a Grade 0 PT (10.3 seconds) at baseline, and an isolated shift to Grade 3 (25.7 seconds) PT on Day 28. All prior assessments of coagulation studies (PT, PTT, and INR) were within reference range. The subject was asymptomatic. Upon repeat testing 6 days later, the value normalized. The investigator indicated that the elevated PT was probably not related to raxibacumab, and that the most likely cause of the event was a laboratory error. This event was recorded as a mild AE (not related, resolved). No other AEs were reported.
L2195: Subject US003-001 (26 year-old white female in Study HGS1021-C1063, raxibacumab single-dose group) had a Grade 0 PT (11.7 seconds) at baseline, and an isolated shift to Grade 3 (23.9 seconds) on Day 28. Concurrent activated PTT (APTT) was Grade 1 (47 seconds). All prior coagulation studies (PT, PTT, and INR) for this subject had been within normal limits. The subject was asymptomatic. On repeat testing 3 days later, the results normalized. This event was recorded as a Grade 3 (severe) AE, which was not related to study agent, and which resolved. The investigator indicated that the most likely cause of the event was an error in specimen collection, processing, or analysis.
L2196: Subject US002-007 (24 year-old white female in Study HGS1021-C1069, raxibacumab post-2nd dose) had fluctuating PT and PTT levels. This subject had a Grade 2 (15.0 seconds) PT at screening and Grade 1 (12.7 seconds) upon rescreeing 6 days later. The subject's PT shifted to Grade 2 (16.7 seconds) on Day 7, decreased to Grade 0 by Day 14, increased again to Grade 3 on Day 42 (17.6 seconds) and Day 56 (27.5 seconds), and further shifted to Grade 4 (37.9 seconds) on Day 70. PT Grades of 2 and 3 respectively were observed at 2 unscheduled assessments done after the end of the
L2197: study period (103 days after raxibacumab dosing). PT had returned to Grade 0 at a post-study, unscheduled assessment performed 112 days after raxibacumab infusion. This subject also had a Grade 0 PTT (32 seconds) at baseline, which shifted to Grade 2 (48 seconds) on Day 70. The PTT had returned to baseline at the unscheduled assessment conducted 112 days after raxibacumab infusion. The subject remained asymptomatic throughout this period and had no complaints of bleeding or easy bruising, and no other clinically significant lab abnormalities. No AEs were reported. The additional laboratory assessments for this subject were conducted to verify the abnormal results, and thus did not trigger the recording of the abnormal laboratory values as AEs at the discretion of the investigator as the subject had no clinical symptoms. No relevant medical history was reported for this subject. The subject moved overseas and was not available for further testing. The laboratory reports were sent to the subject so that she could follow-up with specialists. Relationship to study agent was judged to be probably not related.
L2198: ## Hepatic parameters
L2199: There was 1 subject in Study C1063 (US004-000057) with a grade 3 ALT (304 IU/L, range 0-40 IU/L) on day 56 (16 July 2008). This subject also had a Grade 1 AST elevation of 97 IU/L (range 0-40 IU/L) and a Grade 0 elevation in ALP (154 IU/L, range 25-150 IU/L) on the same day. However, when these tests were repeated on 28 July and 4 Aug 2008, the ALT was 146 IU/L and 57 IU/L and the AST was 90 IU/L and 34 IU/L respectively.
L2200: ## Electrolytes and other laboratory tests
L2201: Subjects treated with 2 raxibacumab doses generally did not have a higher incidence of electrolyte shifts from baseline compared with those treated with a single dose. Time between the 2 raxibacumab doses did not appear to influence the incidence of electrolyte shifts from baseline.
L2202: There were 2 subjects with a shift to Grade 3 or higher laboratory value for electrolytes. Subject US003-004 enrolled in study HGS1021-C1064 was a 51 year-old white male randomized to raxibacumab single dose who had Grade 0 (5.1 mEq/L) potassium level at baseline with an isolated shift to Grade 3 (6.7 mEq/L) on Day 4. This event resolved without treatment and no AEs
L2203: Subject US005-000002 enrolled in C1063 randomized to double dose raxibacumab with a baseline potassium of 8.3 mEq/L (Grade 4) on Day 0. On Study day 1, the level was normal at 4.3 mEq/L and the subject continued in the study. No additional information was available.
L2204: With respect to other laboratory tests, there was 1 subject with a Grade 3 amylase. The narrative is provided below.
L2205: ## Electrolytes and other laboratory tests narratives
L2206: ## Amylase
L2207: Subject US003-002, a 54 year-old white male in Study HGS1021-C1063 (raxibacumab single-dose group) had a Grade 2 amylase level of 159 U/L at screening and a Grade 3 level of 208 U/L on Day 14. The screening value was considered not clinically significant by the investigator. However, the site was not aware of the grading of this value and did enroll the subject; the event was documented as a protocol violation (enrolled but did not meet inclusion/exclusion criteria). The subject was asymptomatic. Repeat assessment on Day 0 was within normal limits (amylase level of 69 U/L). All other relevant laboratory values were within normal limits and the subject was again asymptomatic. On repeat testing, lipase and amylase were within normal limits (lipase 55 U/L, amylase 83 U/L); amylase fractionation was also obtained and found to be within normal limits with no evidence of macroamylasemia. The subject underwent an abdominal ultrasound revealing steatohepatitis, with no stones or wall thickening in the gallbladder, no pericholecystic fluid, and normal pancreas. The findings were determined to be consistent with nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) and considered by the investigator to be not clinically significant. No action was taken with regard to raxibacumab. The investigator indicated that the elevated amylase (severe) was probably not related to raxibacumab. The investigator indicated that there was no clear cause of the asymptomatic recurring elevation in amylase, but that it likely pre-dated exposure to raxibacumab. This event was recorded as a Grade 3 AE (resolved).
L2208: In summary, the incidence of laboratory abnormalities was comparable between raxibacumab-treated and placebo-treated subjects (only active treatment AEs reported here). The incidence was not higher after a second raxibacumab administration than after a single administration. Most lab abnormalities were of low grade (Grade 2 or less), with grade 3 and 4 laboratory abnormalities infrequently reported, isolated and transient.
L2209: ## 7.4.3 Vital Signs
L2210: Three subjects treated with a single raxibacumab dose in study HGS1021-C1063 had AEs of hypertension, which were judged to be not related to raxibacumab. The hypertension was ongoing at the end of the study for 2 subjects. Two additional subjects in the raxibacumab single-dose group had an AE of mild elevated blood pressure, which resolved. The elevated blood pressure for 1 subject was recorded as possibly related to study agent.
L2211: There were 2 reports of fever in study HGS1021-C1063 which were not related to study agent and resolved on study. One case was likely related to a viral infection, as fever was also reported with vomiting and influenza. The remaining case was reported concurrent with headache, both AEs lasted 2 days and resolved without intervention.
L2212: Two AEs of mild tachycardia were reported in Study HGS1021-C1063. Subject US003-000030 was a 18 year old white female with 1 day of palpitations and tachycardia reported on the same day as her single-dose raxibacumab infusion. These AEs were both mild and resolved with no intervention. The second report occurred in a double dose placebo group subject, lasted 1 day with no intervention.
L2213: ## 7.4.4 Electrocardiograms (ECGs)
L2214: Electrocardiograms were obtained prior to enrollment in all studies, and subjects with clinically significant abnormalities were excluded from participation. Telemetric monitoring was performed in Study HGS1021-C1064 prior to dosing of raxibacumab, during the infusion, and for 2 hours following the infusion. No significant arrhythmias during this period were noted. There were no protocol-required subsequent electrocardiograms obtained after the day of raxibacumab infusion in any study.

L2217: ## 7.4.6 Immunogenicity
L2218: ## Non-clinical (Combination animal studies):
L2219: Anti-raxibacumab immunogenicity assessments were added to Study 781-G923701 (NZW rabbits) as a protocol amendment to allow for determination of the impact of any observed anti-raxibacumab immunogenicity on plasma raxibacumab levels and survival.
L2220: Fifteen of 18 rabbits (83%) in the levofloxacin/raxibacumab group tested positive for anti-raxibacumab antibodies on Day 28. In addition, 6/19 (31.6%) rabbits in the levofloxacin group also tested positive for anti-raxibacumab antibodies on Day 28. Although the levofloxacin only treatment group did not receive raxibacumab, the levofloxacin-treated rabbits mounted an anti-PA response which may have included antibodies that cross-reacted in the anti-human anti-PA assay. Given the modest incidence of anti raxibacumab immunogenicity at low titers compared with the raxibacumab-treated animals, this was felt to be a possible explanation proposed by the Applicant. The emergence of potential anti-raxibacumab immunogenicity did not negatively impact survival.
L2221: ## Human
L2222: All 4 human safety studies looked for the development of an anti-raxibacumab antibody response, including PAM-NH-01 which used the M10 formulation of the product. The table below summarizes the time points for immunogenicity assessments in Studies
L2223: HGS1021-C1064, HGS1021-C1063 (second raxibacumab dose 2 weeks following first dose) and HGS1021-C1069 (second dose \ge 4 months following first dose). In all studies, there were no subjects who had a positive anti-raxibacumab antibody response following single or repeat (every 14 days or following \ge 4 months) doses of raxibacumab.

L2227: Immunogenicity testing consisted of screening and confirmatory assays. The screening assay (direct binding) was an electrochemiluminescence (ECL)-based bridging assay, with rabbit polyclonal antibody used as a positive control. Samples identified as positive in the screening assay were to be confirmed positive in a confirmatory assay. The inhibition of binding confirmatory assay was performed identically to the direct binding screening assay with the exception that the samples were tested in parallel with excess unlabeled raxibacumab.
L2228: ## 7.5 Other Safety Explorations
L2229: ## Non-clinical
L2230: In the first ex vivo tissue cross-reactivity studies in humans and cynomolgus monkeys which used the M10 formulation, there was specific binding in skeletal muscle and thyroid in both species, which identified these tissues as possible target organs for toxicity. However, there was no thyroid histopathology or abnormal levels of circulating thyroid hormones in the follow-up study which used the M11 formulation of the product. There were no thyroid AEs reported in the SOC "Metabolism and nutrition disorders".
L2231: ## Clinical
L2232: There were 3 AEs of “blood creatine phosphokinase increased”, one case which was severe and discussed in section 7.3.4 and attributed to increased physical activity. The remaining cases were both coded as mild with no action taken. Subject US005-000021 was a 39 year old white male who received a single dose of raxibacumab in study HGS1021-C1063, while subject US002-000009 enrolled in HGS1021-C1064 was a 18 year old black male who received PO cipro/IV raxi with “exacerbation of CK” 18 days after raxibacumab infusion. The AE was still ongoing at the end of follow-up for the latter subject.
L2233: ## 7.5.1 Dose Dependency for Adverse Events
L2234: ## Non-clinical
L2235: There were no dose-dependent safety findings in the embryo-fetal toxicology study in rabbits (Study 6962-173) or in the chronic toxicology study in cynomolgus monkeys (Study 6962-140). In the histological examination of survivors and nonsurvivors in the anthrax therapeutic efficacy studies the findings were not dose-dependent. Please refer to the Pharmacology/toxicology review for additional details.
L2236: ## Clinical
L2237: With respect to clinical information, data is limited to subjects who got 2 doses of the M11 formulation 2 weeks apart in Study HGS1021-C1063, and those enrolled in PAM-NH-01 (M10 formulation). There were no dose-dependent AEs observed in the former study.
L2238: ## 7.5.2 Time Dependency for Adverse Events
L2239: There was no specific analysis to look for time dependency for adverse events performed as the proposed therapeutic regimen of raxibacumab consists of a single dose.

L2259: ## Age
L2260: The Guidance for Industry: Content and Format for Geriatric Labeling (10) published in 2001 based on the geriatric labeling regulations (CFR 201.57(f)(10) provides standard language for statements in the "Geriatric Use" subsection of the label based on the type of information available and the interpretation of that information. Fewer than 100 geriatric subjects is considered an insufficient number to determine whether these subjects respond differently compared to subjects less than 65 years of age. Of the total number of subjects in clinical studies of raxibacumab, 6.4% (21/326) were 65 and over, while 1.5% (5/326) were 75 and over. Therefore while subset analyses based on age were performed by the Applicant and are presented below, the label will include standard language which states "Clinical studies of raxibacumab did not include sufficient numbers of subjects aged 65 and over to determine whether they respond differently from younger subjects".
L2261: AEs among subjects &lt;65 years of age and ≥65 years of age had similar incidences of AEs as shown in the table below. Subjects &lt; 65 years of age had a higher incidence of Grade 2 AEs compared with subjects ≥65 years of age, although there were many more subjects in the former category (n=305 vs. n=21). There were no severe AEs or SAEs among subjects ≥65 years of age.
L2262: The most frequent AE among subjects &lt; 65 years of age was headache (10.2%). AEs among subjects ≥65 years of age were infrequently reported. The most frequent AEs among subjects ≥65 years of age were in the SOC category for skin and subcutaneous tissue disorders and included AEs of skin pain, rash, and urticaria (1 subject each).

L2269: ## 7.5.4 Drug-Disease Interactions
L2270: ## Non-clinical
L2271: In both NZW rabbit and cynomolgus monkey pivotal efficacy studies, raxibacumab-treated animals that died had more CNS pathology consisting of hemorrhage, necrosis, inflammation and bacteria compared to placebo animals that died. A number of hypotheses were considered investigated, although no clear explanation could be found. Longer survival time may have played some role, but in itself did not account for the increased CNS findings observed primarily in raxibacumab-treated animals.
L2272: In the consult by Dr. Marc Walton, former Director of ODE VI/CDER, he noted that the CNS lesions observed in the pivotal efficacy studies in animal models of inhalational
L2273: anthrax were similar to known manifestations of anthrax infection in animals and humans, and therefore a separate anthrax-unrelated process as the cause of these lesions (i.e., drug-disease interaction) was less likely. In particular, he cited the overall safety of raxibacumab in human studies to date, lack of findings on cross-reactivity studies, and the relative good safety profile of other marketed humanized monoclonal antibody products as evidence against a drug-disease interaction. He further points out that CNS lesions appear to occur only when there is ultimately insufficient treatment to prevent demise, and that death occurs sooner without treatment. For additional analyses and discussion on non-clinical CNS findings, please refer to Section 6.1.5 Analysis of Secondary Endpoints.
L2274: ## 7.5.5 Drug-Drug Interactions
L2275: FDA requested that Studies 781-G923701 and 789-G923702 be conducted to evaluate the effect of raxibacumab on the fluoroquinolones (levofloxacin and ciprofloxacin respectively). The efficacy results suggested that while raxibacumab did not offer additional benefit compared to antibiotics alone, there was no antagonism observed between administration of raxibacumab and antibiotic.
L2276: No other drug-monoclonal interactions have been studied with raxibacumab.
L2277: ## 7.6 Additional Safety Evaluations
L2278: N/A
L2279: ## 7.6.1 Human Carcinogenicity
L2280: No studies have been undertaken to evaluate carcinogenicity or genotoxicity for this fully human immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibody, consistent with the recommendations of ICH S6 (1997).
L2281: Carcinogenicity or genotoxicity studies have not been conducted with raxibacumab.
L2282: ## 7.6.2 Human Reproduction and Pregnancy Data
L2283: There have been no human reproductive and pregnancy studies conducted. An embryo-fetal toxicity study has been conducted in NZW rabbits with negative findings, Please refer to the Pharmacology/toxicology review for details.
L2284: ## 7.6.3 Pediatrics and Assessment of Effects on Growth
L2285: Raxibacumab has not been used in pediatric subjects (subjects \le16 years of age); therefore there is no information on its effects on growth.
L2286: ## 7.6.4 Overdose, Drug Abuse Potential, Withdrawal and Rebound
L2287: There is no clinical experience with overdosage of raxibacumab. In toxicity studies in rabbits and cynomolgus monkeys receiving multiple injections of raxibacumab at 3 to 4 times the recommended dose, there was no raxibacumab-related toxicity. In case of overdosage, it is recommended that the patient be monitored for any signs or symptoms of adverse reactions or effects and appropriate symptomatic treatment instituted immediately.
L2288: The product abuse and dependence potential of raxibacumab has not been examined in nonclinical or clinical studies but is expected to be negligible.
L2289: Withdrawal and rebound are not applicable to raxibacumab as the product is intended for single dose administration.
L2290: ## 7.7 Additional Submissions / Safety Issues
L2291: ## Safety Limitations to Animal Models
L2292: With respect to the pivotal efficacy studies and CNS findings, the main limitation was that survivors were not sacrificed, and therefore no brain histopathology was available to compare with animals that died. While the high efficacy of antibiotics limited the number of animals that died from anthrax in the active treatment arms in both rabbit and NHP combination studies, the rabbit combination study did sacrifice survivors and necropsy was performed on all enrolled animals. While all placebo animals had microscopic findings consistent with anthrax, only 1 animal in an active treatment group died of anthrax (rabbit K99203, levofloxacin group; note rabbit K99246 in the levofloxacin/raxibacumab group died of a gavage accident). CNS analysis was limited as none of the surviving rabbits in the active treatment groups had lesions attributable to anthrax at sacrifice, or any brain lesions on microscopic examination. Therefore, the pathophysiology behind CNS findings observed in the pivotal studies remains to be elucidated. Second, the efficacy of raxibacumab cannot be directly determined in humans. While the animal models have been carefully and extensively tested and characterized, it is still unknown how well they predict efficacy in humans.
L2293: Similar limitations were noted in Study 789-G923702 (ciprofloxacin and raxibacumab in cynomolgus monkeys). No animals in the ciprofloxacin group died during the initial 28
L2294: day time period (monkey C30988 died at 36 days from left leg arterial thrombosis). Only one animal in the ciprofloxacin/raxibacumab treatment group died of anthrax disease (monkey C31142, the other death in this group was due to a gavage error in monkey C24791). None of the surviving animals were sacrificed for histopathologic analysis. As with the rabbit study, the high efficacy of antibiotics and absence of a raxibacumab alone arm limit the degree of analysis for this study.
L2295: With respect to safety as determined in human subjects, a safety database of 326 subjects cannot exclude a SAE or fatal event occurring at less than 1% frequency. In addition, as the safety database consisted only of healthy volunteers, any possible study agent/disease interaction could not be directly assessed. While CNS AEs were reviewed, it appears from the animal models that systemic anthrax disease must be present for CNS pathology to be observed. A review for CNS safety in humans was therefore limited. Other limitations with respect to safety include the exclusion of pediatric subjects and pregnant patients from the safety database. Similarly, non-white subjects represented 28% of the safety database, while subjects greater than 65 years of age represented only 6.4% of subjects; it is unclear whether results of the raxibacumab safety assessment performed for this BLA are generalizable to such populations.

L2297: There is no postmarketing experience available for raxibacumab.

L2308: ## 9.4 Individual Study Reports
L2309: ## **Study Report HGS1021-C1063:** A Randomized, Single-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study to Evaluate the Safety and Tolerability of Raxibacumab (Human Monoclonal Antibody to *B. Anthracis* Protective Antigen) in Healthy Subjects
L2310: Study Phase: 3
L2311: Indication: Therapeutic treatment of inhalational anthrax
L2312: First Subject Enrolled: 12 March 2008
L2313: Last Subject Last Visit: 22 July 2008
L2314: Investigators and Study Centers: Multicenter (6) (US)
L2315: Study Sponsor: Human Genome Sciences, Inc., 14200 Shady Grove Road
Rockville, MD 20850
L2316: ## **Primary Objective**
L2317: - To evaluate the safety and tolerability of IV administered raxibacumab in healthy subjects.
L2318: ## **Secondary Objective**
L2319: - To determine serum raxibacumab concentrations for use in a population PK analysis
L2320: ## **Study Design**
L2321: This was a randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled study of raxibacumab to evaluate the safety and tolerability of raxibacumab administered IV in healthy subjects. Subjects were randomized to 1 of 2 raxibacumab groups (40 mg/kg double-dose administered 14 days apart via IV infusion, or 40 mg/kg IV single dose) or to 1 of 2 matching placebo groups. Subjects were randomized to a treatment group at a ratio of 3:1 (raxibacumab:placebo). All subjects were to be treated with oral diphenhydramine (25-50 mg) up to 60 minutes prior to infusion of raxibacumab.
L2322: Study subjects, investigators and clinical site staff were blinded to treatment assignment. The site pharmacist, study sponsor and Safety Data Monitoring Board were not blinded to treatment assignments.
L2323: The planned treatment groups are shown in the table below.
L2324: **Table: Planned treatment groups** (from Applicant's submission)

Dose 2 - Day 14

Dose 2 - Day 14
2	216	Single-dose raxibacumab	40 mg/kg IV	Single-dose - Day 0

L2327: ## Safety Data Monitoring Board (SMB)
L2328: The SMB met after 100 and then 200 subjects were dosed and evaluated through Day 7 and also reviewed Grade 3 or 4 events or AEs of interest.
L2329: ## Inclusion Criteria
L2330: To be considered eligible to participate in this study, subjects were required to meet the following inclusion criteria:
L2331: - Male or female, \ge 18 years of age.
- Laboratory values that were Grade 0 by the modified Division of Microbiology and Infectious Diseases (DMID) toxicity tables. Subjects with laboratory values that were Grade 1 and were not considered clinically significant by the PI may have been enrolled following consultation with the Medical Monitor.
- A female subject was eligible for this study if she was:Not pregnant or nursing.
- Post menopausal, had a hysterectomy, or documented sterility.
- Of child bearing potential (i.e., a woman with an intact uterus and ovaries and no documentation of oviductal or uterine dysfunction that would cause sterility).
These women must have had a negative blood pregnancy test at screening and on Day 0 prior to randomization and must have agreed to 1 of the following:- Complete abstinence from intercourse from the date of screening through the duration of follow-up.
- Consistent and correct use of 1 of the following medically accepted methods of birth control, in addition to a male partner who correctly used a condom or was sterile prior to the female subject's entry into the study and was the sole sexual partner for the female subject from the date of screening through the duration of follow-up.implants of levonorgestrel;
- injectable progesterone;
- any intrauterine device (IUD) with a documented failure rate of less than 1% per year;
- oral contraceptives (either combined or progesterone only);
- double barrier method: condom, cervical cap or diaphragm with spermicidal agent;
- transdermal contraceptive patch.
- All males who were not sterile must have agreed to either abstain from intercourse or consistently and correctly use a condom while their female partner
L2332: agreed to 1 of the appropriate medically accepted methods of birth control listed above from the date of screening through the duration of follow-up.
L2333: 5. Have the ability to understand the requirements of the study, provide written informed consent (including consent for the use and disclosure of research-related health information), comply with the study protocol procedures, and agree to return for the required study visits.
L2334: ## Exclusion Criteria
L2335: Subjects who met any of the following criteria were excluded:
L2336: 1. History or clinical evidence of significant, acute or chronic diseases, (i.e., cardiovascular, pulmonary, gastrointestinal, hepatic, renal, neurological, or infectious diseases) which could confound the results of the study or put the subject at undue risk.
L2337: 2. Prior immunization with AVA, prior treatment with investigational anthrax therapies, prior treatment for anthrax exposure, or a confirmed anthrax infection.
L2338: 3. History of Type I hypersensitivity reaction to food or drugs, IV contrast agents, antihistamines, or history of urticaria.
L2339: 4. A current drug or alcohol addiction (subjects who had a documented addiction-free period of at least 1 year may have been enrolled based on the clinical judgment of the investigator).
L2340: 5. History of or positive test at the screening visit for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV-1), Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), or Hepatitis C antibody.
L2341: 6. Clinically significant abnormalities in an electrocardiogram (EKG) that would make the subject (in the opinion of the investigator) unsuitable for the study.
L2342: 7. Evidence of active or suspected malignancy or history of malignancy within the last 5 years (with the exception of adequately treated basal cell carcinoma of the skin or in situ carcinoma of the cervix).
L2343: 8. Participation within 60 days of initiating study agent or refusal to refrain from participation during this study in any other clinical trials of an investigational compound.
L2344: 9. Previous exposure to raxibacumab.
L2345: ## Study Schedule
L2346: Subjects who underwent all screening procedures and met the entry criteria were enrolled into the study and assigned a treatment. Randomization was performed on Day 0 prior to administration of the first dose. Subjects randomized to the double dose groups were administered study agent on Days 0 and 14, with follow-up until Day 70 for AEs, while subjects randomized to the single dose groups were administered study agent on Day 0 and followed until Day 56.
L2347: AEs were defined as any unfavorable or unintended sign, symptom, or disease that is temporally associated with the use of a study agent but is not necessarily caused by the study agent. This included worsening (increase in frequency or severity) of pre-existing conditions. Relationship of the AE with the study agent was performed, as well as severity grading using the modified DMID toxicity tables. SAEs were defined in the usual regulatory manner.
L2348: ## Subject Disposition
L2349: The figure below summarizes subject disposition of the 322 randomized subjects in the study. Of the 322 randomized subjects, 320 were treated (72 in the placebo single-dose group, 8 in the placebo double-dose group, 216 in the raxibacumab single-dose group, and 24 in the raxibacumab double-dose group). One subject (US002-004) randomized to the placebo single-dose group had a positive urine drug screen (UDS) and was not dosed per investigator decision. One subject (US005-014) in the raxibacumab single-dose group refused treatment following an unsuccessful initial attempt at venipuncture for IV dosing.

L2361: ## Extent of exposure
L2362: Most subjects got their intended dose, as shown in the table below. In the raxibacumab single-dose group, 2 subjects (US003-016, US003-017) were to have been administered raxibacumab, but no measurable raxibacumab concentrations were obtained at any post dose collections for these subjects. A review of study documentation did not reveal any evidence that these subjects had inadvertently been administered placebo instead of raxibacumab. However, given that high serum raxibacumab levels were attained in other subjects in that dose group, the complete absence of measurable serum raxibacumab concentrations implies that it is very unlikely that these 2 non-evaluable subjects were actually administered a raxibacumab dose.
L2363: One subject randomized to the raxibacumab double-dose group and 2 subjects randomized to the placebo double-dose group did not receive their scheduled second infusion on Day 14 per protocol. Subject US001-009 (raxibacumab double-dose group) reported to the site that he would be unable to comply with the study visits due to work-related obligations. He withdrew from the study due to subject request prior to the next follow-up (Day 7) and thus did not receive the scheduled 2nd dose on Day 14.

L2373: ## Safety evaluation
L2374: ## Treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs)
L2375: A summary of all subjects with at least 1 TEAE is shown in the table below. The incidence of subjects who reported at least 1 AE in this study was comparable among placebo (38/80, 47.5%) and raxibacumab (113/240, 47.1%) treated subjects. In addition, the incidence of at least 1 AE was comparable among subjects in the raxibacumab single-dose (103/217, 47.5%) and raxibacumab double-dose groups (10/23, 43.5%).
L2376: The incidence of SAEs was similarly comparable among placebo and raxibacumab treated subjects. There were 2 SAEs, 1 in the placebo double-dose group and 1 in the raxibacumab double-dose group. In the placebo double-dose group, the SAE was a death that occurred as a result of injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident, an event determined to be not related to study agent. In the raxibacumab double-dose group, a Grade 3 event of cholecystitis occurred and thought to be possibly related to raxibacumab.

L2387: ## TEAEs by PT
L2388: The table below shows TEAEs by SOC and PT, ordered by frequency in the All raxibacumab subjects group. The incidences of the most common AEs in this study were comparable among raxibacumab and placebo-treated subjects, and administration of the 2nd dose of either agent was not associated with a higher incidence of the most common AEs.
L2389: Headache was the most common AE among raxibacumab-treated subjects (20/240, 8.3%), followed by upper respiratory tract infection (13/240, 5.4%). Headache was also the most common AE among placebo-treated subjects (8/80, 10%), followed by upper respiratory tract infection, and pharyngitis (both 4/80, 5.0%). All headaches were mild to moderate in severity, all resolved, and the majority of headaches were not related to study agent. The majority of headaches resolved within 24 hours, and time to onset varied among subjects, with no pattern of clustering around the time of dosing. All AEs of upper respiratory tract infection were mild to moderate in severity, 12 of 13 (92.0%) were not related, and all resolved.
L2390: Based on the occurrence of rash in a prior study (Study HGS1021-C1064), all subjects in the current study received premedication with diphenhydramine, which was well-tolerated. Six of the 240 raxibacumab-treated subjects (2.5% all single-dose subjects) in this study had an AE of rash; 3 were possibly or probably related to raxibacumab. Two of 80 (2.5%) placebo-treated subjects had an AE of rash (both were in the placebo double-dose group; 1 was possibly related). All
L2391: rashes in this study were mild in severity and no action was taken with study agent dosing. All rashes were mild with 2 exceptions (1 in the raxibacumab single-dose group and 1 in the placebo double-dose group [both not related]). Similarly, all were transient with the exception of 1 rash (not related) in a raxibacumab-treated subject (US005-012), which started on Day 45 and was ongoing at the end of the study, and 1 rash (not related) in a placebo-treated subject (US001-002), which started on Day 21 was ongoing at the end of the study.

L2423: ## Subjects with Grade 3 or Higher Hematology Laboratory Values
L2424: The following subjects had a Grade 3 or higher (and a 2-grade shift) hematology laboratory value:
L2425: Subject US004-036 (placebo single-dose group) had Grade 1 (11.47 \times 10^3/\mu\text{L}) WBC count at baseline, which shifted to Grade 3 (20.53 \times 10^3/\mu\text{L}) on Day 1. This event was recorded as a mild AE (not related, resolved). No other AEs were reported.
L2428: Subject US006-030 (raxibacumab single-dose group) had a Grade 0 PT (10.3 seconds) at baseline, and an isolated shift to Grade 3 (25.7 seconds) PT on Day 28. The investigator indicated that the elevated PT was probably not related to raxibacumab, and that the most likely cause of the event was a laboratory error. L2431: ## Liver and Kidney Function
L2432: There was one raxibacumab subject with a grade 3 laboratory value for liver parameters (ALT) with no grades \ge 2 for any other parameters (AST, GGT, ALP or bilirubin). Subject US004-057 (raxibacumab single-dose group) had a Grade 0 ALT of 23 IU/L at baseline, which shifted to Grade 3 (304 IU/L) on Day 56. Other notable laboratory abnormalities for this subject were Grade 1 AST (97 IU/L) and Grade 1 GGT (124 IU/L) also on Day 56. The subject reported symptoms consistent with an upper respiratory tract infection and reported taking over-the-counter medications. ALT of 146 IU/L (Grade 2) and AST of 90 IU/L (Grade 1) were noted upon repeat laboratory assessment on Day 68. On Day 75, ALT decreased to 57 IU/L (Grade 1), and AST decreased to 34 IU/L (Grade 0). No changes were noted in measurements of bilirubin or coagulation studies (PT, PTT). The investigator indicated that the elevated ALT was probably not related to raxibacumab, and that the most likely cause of the event was exposure to other substance. AEs for this subject included myalgia, headache, and sinus congestion (all mild, not related, and resolved).
L2433: ## Electrolytes
L2434: There were no subjects with electrolyte values above Grade 2. There were no 2-grade shifts in electrolytes for subjects in double-dose groups. Six subjects in the raxibacumab single-dose group (1 hypercalcemia and 5 hypophosphatemia) and 1 subject in the placebo single-dose group had a transient shift to Grade 2 electrolytes; all were asymptomatic and no interventions were given.
L2435: ## Other laboratory
L2436: With respect to raxibacumab treated subjects, there were no Grade 3 laboratory tests with the exception of one subject with Grade 3 amylase. Most cases were few reports (less than 5%), and those that were reported at higher frequency, such as Grade 1 hyperglycemia (18.4%) were similar in frequency to the placebo group (placebo hyperglycemia 18.8%). In the Phase 1 study PAM-NH-01 which used the M10 formulation, isolated Grade 2 hypoglycemia was observed in 6 subjects in the IV dose cohorts (1 subject each in the 1 mg/kg [Day 42], 3 mg/kg [Day 28], and 20 mg/kg [Day 14] groups and 3 subjects in the 10 mg/kg group [Day 1, Day 2, and Day 7]). None of these subjects were noted to be symptomatic. The rates of hypoglycemia in the placebo groups vs. the raxibacumab groups were: Grade 1 placebo 6.3%, raxibacumab 5.4%, Grade 2 placebo 2.5%, raxibacumab 2.1% and no cases of Grades 3 or 4 in either group.

L2440: The narrative for the 1 subject with Grade 3 amylase is provided below.

L2449: ## Safety Summary
L2450: Subjects treated with raxibacumab had comparable incidences of AEs, SAEs, or severe AEs compared to placebo treated subjects. Subjects in the raxibacumab double-dose group had a similar incidence of AEs, and SAEs compared to subjects in the raxibacumab single-dose group. Headache (8.3% vs. 10%) and upper respiratory tract infection (5.4% vs. 5.0%) were the most frequently reported AEs in raxibacumab-treated subjects and placebo-treated subjects respectively.
L2451: Two SAEs were reported in this study. One case was a subject in the placebo double-dose group who died due to injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident (not related to study agent), and the other was a Grade 3 event of cholecystitis in the raxibacumab double-dose group. The cholecystitis resolved and was coded as possibly related to raxibacumab as the cholecystitis was most likely caused by progression of concurrent disease. Two subjects, 1 in the placebo double-dose group (skin infection) and 1 in the raxibacumab single-dose group (dyspnea) discontinued treatment due to moderate AEs which resolved.
L2452: The incidence of rash was similar among raxibacumab-treated subjects (2.5%) and placebo-treated subjects (2.5%). Of the 8 incidences of rash, 4 were found to be related to study drug (3 in the raxibacumab single dose group and 1 in the placebo double dose group) and all were transient. Two subjects had a rash that was ongoing at the end of the study (1 subject in the raxibacumab single dose group and 1 subject in the placebo double dose group); both ongoing rashes were not related to study drug.
L2453: Laboratory abnormalities of Grade 3 or higher were infrequently reported in this study. Seven of the 320 subjects in this study (2.2%) had a Grade 3 or higher laboratory abnormality; 6/217 (2.8%) from the raxibacumab single-dose group, and 1/74 (1.4%) from the placebo single-dose group. Hematology laboratory abnormalities above Grade 2 included Grade 3 leukocytosis (1 subject each in the placebo and raxibacumab single-dose groups, Grade 4 neutropenia (1 subject in the raxibacumab single-dose group), and Grade 3 PT (2 subjects in the raxibacumab single-dose group). Chemistry laboratory abnormalities above Grade 2 included Grade 3 ALT and Grade 3 amylase (1 subject each in the raxibacumab single-dose group). All values returned to baseline or to Grade 1 (ALT) prior to completion of study and the events resolved without intervention.
L2454: Incidences of 2-grade shifts in hematology, liver parameters, electrolytes, other chemistries, and urinalysis were comparable between raxibacumab-treated subjects and placebo-treated subjects. Incidences of 2-grade shifts in laboratory values were not higher among subjects in double-dose groups as compared with single dose groups. The majority of 2-grade shifts were transient, not associated with AEs of significance, and required no intervention.
L2455: Lastly, there were no subjects who developed an anti-raxibacumab antibody response during the study.
L2456: ## 9.5 Individual Study Report
L2457: **Study Report HGS1021-C1069:** An Open-Label Study to Evaluate the Immunogenicity and Safety of Raxibacumab (Human Monoclonal Antibody to *B. anthracis* Protective Antigen) Administered in Healthy Subjects
L2458: Study Phase: 2/3
L2459: Indication: Therapeutic treatment of inhalational anthrax
L2460: First Subject Enrolled: 08 January 2008
L2461: Last Subject Last Visit: 08 May 2008
L2462: Investigators and Study Centers: 2 Centers (US)
L2463: Study Sponsor: Human Genome Sciences, Inc., 14200 Shady Grove Road
Rockville, MD 20850
L2464: ## Primary Objective
L2465: To evaluate immunogenicity in subjects receiving 2 doses of raxibacumab with a delay prior to the 2nd dose.
L2466: ## Secondary Objectives
L2467: - To evaluate safety in subjects receiving 2 doses of raxibacumab with a delay prior to the 2nd dose.
- To determine serum raxibacumab PK in subjects receiving 2 doses of raxibacumab with a delay prior to the 2nd dose.
L2468: ## Study Design
L2469: This was a single-group, open-label study to evaluate the immunogenicity and safety of raxibacumab in healthy adult male and female subjects. Subjects who had received raxibacumab \ge 4 months prior to this study in Study HGS1021-C1064 were eligible for enrollment. The longest half-life for the terminal elimination phase for any subject administered an IV raxibacumab dose in the Phase 1 study PAM-NH-01 was 26.4 days. This justified selection of a 4-month washout period between raxibacumab doses in this study, as this ensured that more than 95% of the 1st dose would be eliminated before the 2nd dose was administered.
L2470: In Study HGS1021-C1064, 3 treatment groups were evaluated:
L2471: **Group 1:** 15 doses of PO ciprofloxacin (500 mg every 12 hours) from Day 0 to Day 7. On Day 5, prior to the 1st daily ciprofloxacin dose, the subjects were also to receive a single dose of raxibacumab (40 mg/kg) IV.
L2472: Group 2: a single dose of raxibacumab (40 mg/kg) IV on Day 0.
L2473: Group 3: One dose of IV ciprofloxacin (400 mg) on Day 0 immediately followed by IV raxibacumab (40 mg/kg). A 2nd dose of IV ciprofloxacin (400 mg) was to be administered on Day 0, 12 hours after the 1st infusion was completed. Subjects in Group 3 were to continue with PO ciprofloxacin (500 mg Q12h) on Days 1 to 7 for a total of 13 doses.
L2474: For the current study, a maximum of 25 subjects (to include at least 3 evaluable female subjects) were to receive a 2nd dose of raxibacumab 40 mg/kg IV \ge4 months following their 1st dose. Subjects were to remain in the clinical unit from Day 0 until Day 1 and were followed for 70 days after receiving their 2nd dose of raxibacumab.
L2475: ## Inclusion Criteria
L2476: - Enrolled and treated with raxibacumab in another HGS protocol \ge4 months ago.
- Male or female \ge18 and \le64 years of age.
- Laboratory values that were Grade 0 by the modified Division of Microbiology and Infectious Diseases (DMID) toxicity tables. Subjects with laboratory values that were Grade 1 and were not considered clinically significant by the principal investigator may have been enrolled following consultation with the medical monitor.
- A female subject was eligible to enter the study if she was:Not pregnant or nursing.
- Post menopausal, had a hysterectomy, or documentation of sterility.
- Of child-bearing potential (i.e., woman with an intact uterus and ovaries and no documentation of oviductal or uterine dysfunction that would cause sterility).
These women must have had a negative blood pregnancy test at screening and on Day -1 prior to dosing and agree to 1 of the following:

- Complete abstinence from intercourse from the date of screening through the duration of follow-up.
- Consistent and correct use of 1 of the following medically accepted methods of birth control, in addition to a male partner who correctly used a condom or was sterile prior to the female subject's entry into the study and was the sole sexual partner for the female subject from the date of screening through the duration of follow-up:implants of levonorgestrel.
- injectable progesterone.
- any intrauterine device (IUD) with a documented failure rate of less than 1% per year.
- oral contraceptives (either combined or progesterone only).
- double barrier method: condom, cervical cap or diaphragm with spermicidal agent.
- transdermal contraceptive patch.
L2477: - All males who were not sterile must have agreed to either abstain from intercourse or consistently and correctly use a condom while their female partner agreed to use 1 of the appropriate medically accepted methods of birth control listed above from the date of screening through the duration of follow-up.
- Have the ability to understand the requirements of the study, provide written informed consent (including consent for the use and disclosure of research-related health information), comply with the study protocol procedures, and agree to return for the required study visits.
L2478: ## Exclusion Criteria
L2479: - History or clinical evidence of significant, acute, or chronic diseases (i.e., cardiovascular, pulmonary, gastrointestinal, hepatic, renal, neurological, or infectious diseases), which could have confounded the results of the study or put the subject at undue risk.
- Prior immunization with AVA, prior treatment with investigational anthrax therapies (other than raxibacumab \ge 4 months ago), prior treatment for anthrax exposure, or a confirmed anthrax infection.
- History of Type I hypersensitivity reaction to food or drugs, IV contrast dye, or history of urticaria.
- Previous hypersensitivity to raxibacumab.
- Previous serious or Grade 3 or greater raxibacumab-related AE.
- Drug or alcohol addiction within the last 12 months. Subjects who had a documented addiction-free period of at least 12 months and in the clinical judgment of the investigator were not at risk for relapse may have been enrolled in the study.
- Evidence of active or suspected malignancy or history of malignancy within the last 5 years (with the exception of adequately treated basal cell carcinoma of the skin or in situ carcinoma of the cervix).
- Participation in any other clinical trials of an investigational compound (other than raxibacumab \ge 4 months prior) within 60 days of initiating study agent or refusal to refrain from participation during this study.
L2480: ## Treatments Administered
L2481: Eligible subjects were to receive a 2nd dose of raxibacumab by IV infusion equal to that of their previous dose \ge 4 months following the 1st dose (all subjects were treated with a 40 mg/kg raxibacumab dose). All subjects were to be treated with 50 mg oral (PO) diphenhydramine up to 60 minutes prior to infusion of raxibacumab.
