L2494: ## Immunogenicity testing and Assay Methods
L2495: Immunogenicity testing was performed to determine if raxibacumab induced an anti-raxibacumab immune response. Subjects with a positive anti-raxibacumab antibody response anytime following the 2nd dose were to have a serum sample collected approximately 6 months after the last dose for a follow-up immunogenicity assessment.
L2496: Testing comprised 2 assays (screening and confirmatory). The screening assay (direct binding) was an electrochemiluminescence (ECL)-based bridging assay, with rabbit polyclonal antibody used as a positive control. Samples above the assay cut point were considered positive. Samples identified as positive in the screening assay were to be confirmed positive in a confirmatory assay. Samples must have demonstrated a significant percent drop in the confirmatory inhibition of binding assay to be considered positive. The inhibition of binding confirmatory assay was performed identically to the direct binding screening assay with the exception that the samples were tested in parallel with excess unlabeled raxibacumab. The assay limit of detection was 62.5 ng/mL.
L2497: ## Adverse Events
L2498: An AE was defined as any unfavorable or unintended sign, symptom, or disease that is temporally associated with the use of a study agent but is not necessarily caused by the study agent. This included worsening of pre-existing conditions. All AEs and serious AEs (SAEs) that were identified from study agent administration on Day 0 through end of study (Day 70) were recorded on the AE CRF. The record of each AE on the CRF included AE description or diagnosis, start date, end date, whether the AE was ongoing, whether any medication was taken, seriousness, severity, action taken with study agent, relationship to study agent (causality), and outcome.
L2499: ## Severity Grading
L2500: The investigator evaluated all AEs with respect to severity using the modified DMID Toxicity Tables. For AEs that were not included in the modified DMID Toxicity Tables, the following guidelines applied:
L2501: - Mild - causing no limitation of usual activities
- Moderate - causing some limitation of usual activities
- Severe - causing inability to carry out usual activities
- Life Threatening* - potentially life threatening or disabling
L2502: ## Serious Adverse Events
L2503: An SAE was defined as any AE resulting in any of the following outcomes:
L2504: - death.
- was life threatening (i.e., an immediate threat to life).
- inpatient hospitalization.
- prolongation of an existing hospitalization.
- persistent or significant disability/incapacity.
- congenital anomaly/birth defect.
- was medically important.
L2505: ## Follow-up of AEs and SAEs
L2506: AEs that occurred from the start of study agent administration on Day 0 through End of Study (Day 70) were followed until final outcome was known or until the end of the study if the event was ongoing. AEs that had not resolved by the end of the study were recorded as ongoing. SAEs that had not resolved by the end of the study were to be followed until final outcome was known. If it was not possible to obtain a final outcome for an SAE (e.g., the subject was lost to follow-up), the reason that a final outcome could not be obtained was to be documented by the investigator.

L2515: ## Protocol Amendments
L2516: ## Changes Resulting from Amendment 01 (16 October 2007)
L2517: - A requirement for in-house observation for 24 hours following dosing and telemetric monitoring during study agent infusion was added at the request of the FDA.
- Wording for the inclusion criterion that subjects were to have been previously treated with raxibacumab in the last 4-6 months was changed to specify that the
L2518: subjects were to have been previously treated with raxibacumab at least 4 months prior to the planned dose for this study.
L2519: - A period of at least 4 months or greater was sufficient to ensure that more than 95% of the 1st raxibacumab dose had been eliminated. Inclusion of subjects who were dosed \ge 4 months ago would allow subjects from previous HGS protocols to be included.
L2520: - Wording was changed to specify that “subjects will receive raxibacumab at a dose equal to that of the 1st dose rather than specifying 40 mg/kg raxibacumab for a 2nd dose.”
L2521: - This change was to allow potential inclusion of subjects who might have received other raxibacumab doses in HGS protocols.
L2522: - Blood alcohol and urine drug tests were removed from the study schedule.
L2523: - Exposure to alcohol or drugs was not expected to affect the results of this trial.
L2524: - Procedures to mitigate anticipated and observed infusion reactions were added at the request of FDA.
L2525: - The following text was added: “If an infusion reaction occurs, the infusion should be slowed or interrupted and treatment administered based on the severity of the reactions. Subjects will be strongly encouraged to notify medical staff immediately if they develop any sign of infusion reaction.”
L2526: - The post raxibacumab infusion follow-up period was changed from 90 days to 70 days.
L2527: - New immunogenicity qualification experiments demonstrated that in the presence of the predicted concentration of raxibacumab on Day 70 post infusion (16.6 \mu\text{g/mL}), the assay was able to reliably detect less than 1.0 \mu\text{g/mL} of anti-drug antibody. In the presence of the predicted concentration of raxibacumab on Day 90 post infusion (5.7 \mu\text{g/mL}) the assay was able to reliably detect less than 0.5 \mu\text{g/mL} of anti-drug antibody. As the difference in sensitivity was minor, these findings supported moving the last time point from Day 90 to Day 70.
L2528: - New information on study agent background and data management was added, including:
L2529: - Preliminary results of a Good Laboratory Practices (GLP) rabbit embryo-fetal toxicity study, in which no adverse effects of raxibacumab on embryo/fetal viability and growth and no maternal toxicity occurred.
L2530: - Safety and PK results obtained in a study of healthy volunteers co-administered raxibacumab and ciprofloxacin (HGS1021-C1064).
L2531: - Additional details on how CRFs were completed, reviewed by the investigator, retrieved by the sponsor, and processed by the sponsor's Data Management department were added.

L2563: Two subjects had Grade 2 hematology values. Subject US002-007 had fluctuating prothrombin time (PT) and partial thromboplastin time (PTT) values. This subject had a Grade 2 PT at screening and Grade 1 upon rescreening 1 week later. The subject's PT shifted to Grade 2 on Day 7, decreased to Grade 0 by Day 14, increased again to Grades 3 and 4 (27.5 seconds) on Days 42 and Day 56 and further shifted to Grade 4 (37.9 seconds) on Day 70. PT Grades of 2 and 3 were observed at 2 unscheduled assessments done after the end of the study period (103 days after raxibacumab dosing). PT had returned to Grade 0 at a post-study, unscheduled assessment performed 112 days after raxibacumab infusion. This subject also had a Grade 0 PTT (32 seconds) at baseline, which shifted to Grade 2 on Day 70. The PTT had returned to baseline at the unscheduled assessment conducted 112 days after raxibacumab infusion. The subject remained asymptomatic throughout this period and had no complaints of bleeding or easy bruising, and no other clinically significant lab abnormalities. No AEs were reported. The additional laboratory assessments for this subject were conducted to verify the abnormal results, and thus did not trigger the recording of the abnormal laboratory values as AEs at the discretion of the investigator as the subject was without clinical symptoms. No relevant medical history was reported for this subject. The subject moved overseas and was not available for further testing. Relationship to study agent was judged to be probably not related.
L2564: Subject US002-013 had a normal white blood cell count at baseline, and an isolated Grade 2 lymphopenia on Day 70. All other assessments for this subject were Grade 0. No concurrent AEs were reported.

L2575: ## Vital Signs and Physical Exam

L2577: ## Safety Summary
L2578: Safety findings were limited in this study. There were no deaths, SAEs, AEs of severe intensity, or subjects who discontinued raxibacumab treatment due to AEs. All AEs were transient, mild to moderate in severity, and resolved. The
L2579: relationship of these AEs to raxibacumab was deemed to be not related or probably not related in all instances.
L2580: With respect to immunogenicity, no subjects in this study developed an anti-raxibacumab antibody response.
L2581: With respect to laboratory tests, there were a small number of transient shifts to Grade 2 or higher clinical laboratory values in this study with no consistent pattern of change, and there were no temporally associated AEs or symptoms reported. There were few changes in hematology and liver and kidney laboratory parameters.

Submission Title:	Evaluation of the Efficacy of Raxibacumab in Combination with Ciprofloxacin for Therapeutic Treatment in the Cynomolgus Monkey Inhalation Anthrax Model (Battelle Study 789-G923702)
L2584: Evaluation of the Efficacy of Raxibacumab in Combination with Ciprofloxacin for Therapeutic Treatment in the Cynomolgus Monkey Inhalation Anthrax Model
L2585: **STUDY DIRECTOR:** Daniel Sanford, Ph.D.
L2586: **STUDY ASSOCIATE DIRECTOR:** Jason M. Mott, DVM, Ph.D.
L2587: **STUDY CENTER:** Battelle Biomedical Research Center (BBRC)
L2588: **STUDY PERIOD:** February 18, 2008 to March 6, 2009
L2589: **REPORT DATE:** March 26, 2009
L2590: **STUDY PROCEDURE:** Study was conducted under GLP
L2591: ## **OBJECTIVES:**
L2592: ## **Primary Objective:**
L2593: To evaluate the efficacy of raxibacumab when administered as a therapeutic agent in combination with ciprofloxacin against lethality due to inhalation exposure of *B. anthracis* in cynomolgus monkeys
L2594: ## **Additional Objectives:**
L2595: To determine the pharmacokinetics (PK) of intragastric (IG) ciprofloxacin doses and of an intravenous (IV) raxibacumab dose when co-administered, as well as the kinetics of *B. anthracis* protective antigen (PA), in monkeys with inhalation anthrax
L2596: **METHODOLOGY:** Parallel-group, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study to evaluate the efficacy of raxibacumab in combination with ciprofloxacin as a therapeutic treatment in cynomolgus monkeys with inhalation anthrax
L2597: **NUMBER OF ANIMALS:** 40 naïve cynomolgus monkeys were randomized into 2 separate treatment groups of 14 animals and a placebo group of 12 monkeys (each 50% male and 50% female). Three animals were held as replacements but were not used.
L2598: **STUDY DRUG:** Treatment with study agent was triggered upon detection of serum PA via the screening assay or at 54 hours post-challenge. Ciprofloxacin (75 mg) or control material (sterile water for injection, WFI) was administered IG for 6 doses: initially once the criterion for treatment was met and then every (Q) 12 hours (\pm 1 hour) for 5 doses. In addition, a single IV bolus dose of raxibacumab (40 mg/kg) or raxibacumab buffer (1 mL/kg) was administered immediately after administration of the first ciprofloxacin dose. Within 5 minutes prior to treatment each monkey received a single 1 mg/kg intramuscular (IM) dose of diphenhydramine to parallel the treatment paradigm for humans in Phase 2/3 studies.
L2599: Raxibacumab is a recombinant, fully human IgG1\lambda mAb that binds PA with high affinity and inhibits its biological activity. Raxibacumab is expressed in the NS0 mouse myeloma cell line, secreted into culture media, and purified by a series of chromatography and filtration steps. Raxibacumab was supplied by HGS as a
L2600: ready-to-use sterile liquid formulation (50 mg/mL) in a formulation buffer of 0.13 mg/mL citric acid, 2.8 mg/mL sodium citrate, 10 mg/mL sucrose, 18 mg/mL glycine, 0.2 mg/mL polysorbate 80, pH 6.5. Storage was at 2-8°C in the dark. During dosage periods the bottles were to be wrapped to keep in the dark and stored on ice. A certificate of analysis and stability data was provided by the sponsor. Raxibacumab from lot 71044 was used.
L2601: Ciprofloxacin (Cipro® IV, 10 mg/mL) was obtained from a commercial source (Bayer Health Care Pharmaceuticals, Inc., Wayne, NJ). Records of the ciprofloxacin lot number, expiration date, and storage conditions were retained in the study record. A ciprofloxacin dose equivalent to a 500 mg human dose was used in this study. The ciprofloxacin dose was calculated using the relative body surface area of the rhesus monkey, with body surface area estimated from body weight. Taking a midpoint in the body weight of cynomolgus monkeys, a dose of 75 mg was calculated using a similar approach. Ciprofloxacin Batch 5400PLX was used.
L2602: Placebo for raxibacumab was raxibacumab buffer, administered at 1 mL/kg. Placebo from Lot 71043 was used. The placebo for ciprofloxacin was sterile WFI (Lot 710375F (b)(4)), and was administered IG.
L2603: All monkeys received a single IM dose of diphenhydramine (1 mg/mL) within 5 minutes prior to study agent administration.
L2604: **DURATION OF TREATMENT:** A single dose of raxibacumab or raxibacumab buffer was given on Day 0. Ciprofloxacin or sterile WFI was given every 12 hours for a total of 6 doses.
L2605: **STUDY DESIGN:** This was a parallel-group, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled GLP study to evaluate the efficacy of raxibacumab in combination with ciprofloxacin as a therapeutic treatment in the cynomolgus monkey inhalation anthrax model. PA kinetics and raxibacumab and ciprofloxacin PK were also examined.
L2606: Forty (50% male, 50% female) juvenile (&lt; 5 years of age) cynomolgus macaques (*Macaca fascicularis*) weighing between 2.0 to 6.0 kg at randomization were randomized into 3 treatment groups (see Table 1 below), and randomly assigned to 1 of 3 aerosol challenge days and a challenge order.

L2609: **Table 1. Treatment Groups**
L2610: On Day 0, monkeys were aerosol challenged with a targeted 200 x LD50 [1.24 \times 10^7 spores] dose of *B. anthracis* spores (Ames strain) aerosolized by a Collison nebulizer and delivered via a head-only inhalation exposure chamber. Treatment with study agent was triggered upon detection of serum PA via the ECL screening assay or at 54 hours post-challenge. Ciprofloxacin (75 mg) or control material (sterile water for injection, WFI) was administered IG for 6 doses: initially once the criterion for treatment was met and then every (Q) 12 hours (\pm 1 hour) for 5 doses. In addition, a single IV bolus dose of raxibacumab (40 mg/kg) or raxibacumab buffer (1 mL/kg) was administered immediately after administration of the first ciprofloxacin dose. Within 5 minutes prior to treatment each monkey received a single 1 mg/kg intramuscular (IM) dose of diphenhydramine to parallel the treatment paradigm for humans in Phase 2/3 studies. Staff members administering study agents were blinded to study agent preparation to preclude introduction of bias into the study following treatment.
L2611: **MO comment:** The raxibacumab treatment in the monkeys was administered as a bolus injection. In human studies, raxibacumab is to be administered by infusion over 2.5 hours. This difference in administration times needs to be taken into account in matching the animal and human PK parameters, especially related to Cmax.
L2612: Monkeys were observed every 6 hours beginning 24 hours post median challenge time and ending 192 hours (8 days) post median challenge time for clinical signs including, but not limited to, anorexia, lethargy, respiratory distress, moribundity, activity (recumbent, weak, or unresponsive), seizures, and other abnormal clinical observations, after which they were observed twice daily, or more often if there was any sign of distress. Monkeys surviving the post-challenge could be returned to the sponsor (if required) or donated following observation for an additional 60 days under BL-2 laboratory conditions for recrudescence. Gross necropsy was performed on all monkeys that were found dead or were euthanized. Histopathology was to be performed, as deemed necessary by a board-certified veterinary pathologist, to confirm death or illness due to anthrax. Blood samples were collected on the days specified in Table 5-3 for hematology and CRP, as well as to measure bacteremia by culture, serum PA levels, anti-PA and TNA levels, serum raxibacumab levels and ciprofloxacin levels.
L2613: **Inclusion criteria:**
L2614: - Male and female juvenile (&lt; 5 years of age) naïve Chinese colony bred cynomolgus monkeys by (b) (4).
- Weight 2.0 to 6.0 kg at randomization.
- Free of malformations and clinical signs of disease.
- Monkeys were to be tested and verified negative for tuberculosis and screened within 30 days prior to receipt at Battelle and found to be negative for Simian Immunodeficiency Virus, Simian T-Lymphotrophic Virus-1 (STLV-1), and *Cercopithecine herpesvirus* 1 (Herpes B virus). All monkeys were required to be tested negative for Simian Retrovirus (SRV1 and SRV2) by polymerase chain reaction (PCR).
L2615: ## Exclusion criteria:
L2616: - Malformations.
- Clinical signs and symptoms of disease.
- Any monkeys outside the specified weight range.
- Any monkey with any one of the infections listed above.
L2617: ## Euthanasia Criteria:
L2618: Any of the following criteria prompted immediate euthanasia:
L2619: - Presence of any seizure denoting primary central nervous system disease.
- Respiratory distress, dyspnea, or forced abdominal respirations.
- Unresponsive to touch or external stimuli.
- Moribundity.
L2620: Euthanasia was warranted when all the clinical signs below were observed:
L2621: - Recumbence and weakness.
- \ge 20\% body weight loss.
- Body temperature below 97°F; indicative of shock.
- Total anorexia with duration longer than 48 hours.
L2622: All monkeys that were judged to be moribund by a highly trained life sciences technician, Battelle veterinarian, or by the study director were euthanized immediately. Euthanasia was accomplished by anesthetizing with Telazol (1-6 mg/kg) IM, collecting blood if possible for tests, and immediate euthanasia using an overdose of a barbiturate that is administered IV or by intracardiac injection or other American Veterinary Medical Association (AVMA) approved method of euthanasia.
L2623: ## Aerosol Challenge:
L2624: On Day 0, monkeys were anesthetized with Telazol (1-6 mg/kg, IM) and placed into a plethysmography chamber and a Class III cabinet system. Monkeys were aerosol-challenged with a targeted 200 x LD50 [1.24 x 107 spores] dose of *B. anthracis* spores (Ames strain) aerosolized by a Collison nebulizer and delivered via a head-only inhalation exposure chamber.
L2625: ## Randomization of Monkeys:
L2626: Forty-three naïve cynomolgus macaques were randomized into 1 group of 12 animals,
L2627: 2 groups of 14 animals (all 3 groups having 50% female, 50% male), and 1 group of 3 replacement animals (all male), and then into 3 aerosol challenge sets of animals. The 3 sets of monkeys were aerosol challenged on 3 staggered challenge days (Day 0). Randomizations were performed with SAS® statistical software.
L2628: ## Treatments and Study Groups:
L2629: Cynomolgus monkeys were randomized to one of three aerosol challenge days and a challenge order per day. On day 0, monkeys were challenged with a targeted aerosol dose of 200 \times \text{LD}_{50} spores of *B. anthracis* (Ames strain). For individual monkeys, treatment was to be administered immediately following detection of serum PA via the PA screening assay. Animals that did not have a positive serum PA screening assay result by 54 hours post challenge were to be treated with their intended treatment (because additional screening was not possible due to blood collection limits). Within 5 minutes prior to treatment each monkey was to receive a single 1 mg/kg IM dose of diphenhydramine to reflect the proposed treatment paradigm in humans.
L2630: ## Blinding:
L2631: Staff administering raxibacumab and raxibacumab buffer and/or conducting assessments of monkeys post challenge were to be blinded to their treatment assignments. Pathologists and the technicians performing the bacteremia cultures were also blinded to treatment group assignment. BBRC personnel not involved with the treatment or assessment of monkeys were to aseptically dilute raxibacumab with raxibacumab buffer to assure that the volume of raxibacumab and raxibacumab buffer were equal. A BBRC staff member who was not associated with the conduct of the study was to randomly assign vial identifications to each of the 3 treatment groups. Dilutions of study raxibacumab and raxibacumab buffer were to be sealed in sterile dosing vials labeled X, Y, or Z (only 1 vial identification was to be used for the dilutions of study agent; the other 2 were to be used for the control material). Dilutions of study agent and transfer of control material were to be performed no earlier than 3 days prior to challenge and were to be stored at 2-8°C in the dark prior to dosing. Vial assignments were to be maintained by Battelle's Quality Assurance Unit until 32 days following the 3rd challenge day.
L2632: ## Clinical Observations:
L2633: The study duration was 28 days, with an additional post-Day 28 observation period of 60 days. Monkeys were to be observed every 6 hours beginning 24 hours post median challenge time and ending 192 hours (8 days) post median challenge time for clinical signs including, but not limited to, anorexia, lethargy, respiratory distress, moribundity, activity (recumbent, weak, or unresponsive), seizures, and other
L2634: abnormal clinical observations. Should any animals have been documented as having respiratory distress or as being unresponsive during the 8 days following challenge, more frequent observations may have been performed and telemetry data may have been reviewed to determine if body temperature or activity levels were decreasing. Any additional observations were to be documented at the time of the observation. If at the final clinical observation on Day 8 no animal was exhibiting unresponsiveness or respiratory distress, observations performed every 6 hours were to cease and animals were to be observed twice daily thereafter. In addition, appetite was to be monitored twice daily during this observation period. During the quarantine and prechallenge period and from Day 9 through Day 32 post-exposure, clinical observations were to be recorded twice daily. Observed signs of illness or live/found dead/euthanized animals were to be recorded at the time of the observation. Any animal judged by a trained animal technician or study veterinarian to be moribund (in consultation with the study director) may have undergone, if possible, a terminal blood draw collected in ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) and serum separator (SST) tubes for bacteremia, serum PA analysis, and CRP.
L2635: ## Necropsy and Histopathology:
L2636: Gross necropsy was to be performed on all monkeys that were found dead or were euthanized. Sections of target tissues, including but not limited to brain/meninges, lungs, liver, spleen, kidney, and mediastinal lymph nodes as well as all gross lesions, were to be preserved in 10% neutral buffered formalin. Histopathology was to be performed, as deemed necessary by a board-certified veterinary pathologist, to confirm death or illness due to anthrax. Representative samples of spleen, liver, and mediastinal lymph node were to be collected during gross necropsy, homogenized, and plated on blood agar plates for qualitative assessment of bacterial presence in the target tissues. The study pathologist was to be blinded to the treatment group assignment until all necropsy and histopathology study activities were completed. In order to confirm a cause of death or moribundity, tissues from all animals that died on study were processed to approximately 5-micron sections for routine hematoxylin and eosin staining and were examined microscopically by a board-certified veterinary pathologist. Diagnoses were entered into the PATH/TOX SYSTEM (Xybion Medical Systems Corporation) data management system for data recording and analysis. Due to the study blinding requirement, treatment groups were randomly relabeled X, Y and Z, and the pathologist had no knowledge of the associated treatment for any animal. Photos of relevant microscopic lesions were obtained and included in electronic form in the study file.
L2637: **MO comment:** Histopathology analysis was performed on all animals that died, in response to the FDA request in amendment 4 (November 10, 2008) of the protocol.
L2638: ## **Blood Collection and Testing:**
L2639: Blood samples were to be taken from a femoral artery or vein, saphenous vein, or other appropriate vein on the days specified in Table 2 below. All post challenge pretreatment blood samples were to be collected relative to the median challenge time at the timepoints stated (\pm 1 hour). Median challenge time was to be calculated from the end time of the 1st and last animals challenged within a single challenge day. Blood collections were to be scheduled based on their post challenge or posttreatment times, as indicated. All posttreatment blood samples were to be collected relative to the end time of each animal's raxibacumab (or raxibacumab buffer) treatment. Exact blood draw times were to be documented. The number of blood samples collected may have been reduced if it was determined by the study director in consultation with a Battelle veterinarian that additional collections would have significantly compromised the animal's health. Should this have occurred, documentation was to be included in the study file, and analyses limited to those samples collected.

L2643: Post challenge pretreatment bleed timepoints were to be relative to a median challenge time for a challenge cohort. Post-treatment bleed times were to be calculated from the time each animal's IV treatment ended. Blood samples were to occur within \pm 60 minutes of the calculated time, except for the first 2 post-treatment blood samples, which were to occur within 5 and 15 minutes of the calculated time, respectively. The Day 8, Day 14, Day 21, and Day 28 post challenge blood samplings were to be
L2644: relative to the day of challenge. Body temperatures and activity were to be monitored at least hourly beginning 10-14 days prior to challenge, and until the end of the in-life animal phase (32 days post challenge). Body temperatures were to be recorded via TA-D70 telemetry transmitters (DSI, St. Paul, MN) after surgical implantation, which was conducted during quarantine.
L2645: 1 Blood specimens for anti-PA antibodies and TNA were to be collected from all monkeys at 7 days prior to spore challenge as well as 28 days after spore challenge. The blood specimens were allowed to clot and were then centrifuged. The serum was harvested, filtered, cultured for presence of *B. anthracis*, and stored at \le 70^{\circ}\text{C} prior to shipment to HGS for assay. If sufficient volume for the 14 and 21 days post spore challenge specimens remained, those specimens may also have been analyzed for anti-PA antibody and TNA.
L2646: 2 Processing to serum was to be initiated within 60 minutes of collection.
L2647: ## Assays:
L2648: For assessment of bacteremia by culture, approximately 40 \mu\text{L} of whole blood or tissue homogenate (prepared in 2 mL of phosphate buffered saline) was to be collected in EDTA tubes, streaked on blood agar plates, and incubated at approximately 37^{\circ}\text{C} for a minimum of 48 hours per SOP BBRC.X-096. Following incubation, macroscopic observations were to be performed to assess the presence or absence of bacterial colonies. Colonies were to be assessed for hemolysis type, size, color, and morphology. If \gamma-hemolytic, white colonies, 4-10 mm in diameter with a rough appearance and irregular edges were present, the sample was to be documented as positive for *B. anthracis*.
L2649: For levofloxacin and ciprofloxacin MICs, serial dilutions of levofloxacin and ciprofloxacin were to be prepared in sterile water and added to a volume of sterile media in microplates for a final concentration of 0.0156 to 32 \mu\text{g}/\text{mL}. A dilution of the *B. anthracis* inoculum was to be prepared in sterile broth and used to inoculate the microplates. The microplates were to be incubated at approximately 37^{\circ}\text{C} for approximately 16 to 20 hours. Macroscopic observations were to be performed to assess the level of growth (turbidity) and determine the MIC of the antibiotics. The MIC was recorded as the lowest concentration of drug resulting in no visible growth.
L2650: Hematology evaluation was performed with the Advia® 120. Hematology slides were to be prepared and reviewed when necessary as determined by a highly-trained hematology technician or the Study Director. Hematology parameters that were monitored may have included but was not limited to: WBC, differential leukocyte count, RBC, hemoglobin, hematocrit, MCV, MCH, MCHC, RDW, platelets, MPV, and neutrophil to lymphocyte number ratio. CRP analysis was to be performed on residual plasma collected from each whole blood sample after processing, with no repeat analysis. CRP analysis was also to be conducted on terminal blood samples collected in EDTA tubes if the plasma could be isolated.
L2651: CRP analysis was a non-validated assay run according to the manufacturer's instructions.
L2652: Serum PA screening assay was an ECL based assay. Undiluted serum samples in triplicate wells were to be incubated in the presence of rabbit anti-PA-biotin and rabbit anti-PA-SULFOTAG for 2 hours at 37°C in a streptavidin-coated assay plate. The limit of detection was established at 1.0 ng/mL based on the qualification experiments. Total PA (free + raxibacumab-bound) concentrations in serum samples were determined using an ECL-based bridging assay (SOP CLI-2996). Diluted serum samples in duplicate wells were combined with monkey polyclonal antibody (pAb) anti-PA-biotin (capture) and monkey pAb anti-PA-SULFO-TAG (detector) and allowed to equilibrate in a streptavidin-coated assay plate. Following equilibration, plates were washed and read for ECL counts. The concentration of PA in serum samples and controls was interpolated from a reference standard curve. The assay was required to have met system suitability criteria to be valid. The lower limit of quantitation (LLOQ) was 0.65 ng/mL of PA in 100% monkey serum.
L2653: Anti-PA antibody concentrations in serum samples were to be determined using an ELISA. Anti-PA antibody was to be captured on wild-type PA coated plates and the concentration was interpolated from a reference standard curve. The lower limit of quantification was &lt; 600 ng/mL of anti-PA antibodies in 100% monkey serum.
L2654: TNA titers were to be determined using a cell killing assay in J744A.1 macrophages. Inhibition of PA binding is correlated with increased cell viability and is used to determine the relative titer of serum samples compared with a known positive control. The lower limit of quantification was &lt; 52 titer in 100% monkey serum.
L2655: Serum samples were analyzed for raxibacumab using an ECL-based assay where raxibacumab in serum binds to the biotinylated-PA on a streptavidin-coated plate and is detected by the addition of rabbit anti-raxibacumab antibody followed by goat anti-rabbit antibody labeled with MSD SULFOTAG. The concentration was interpolated from a reference standard curve. The lower limit of quantification was 940 ng/mL in 100% monkey serum.
L2656: Serum samples were analyzed for ciprofloxacin at CSU, using a high performance liquid chromatography/mass spectrometry/mass spectrometry (LC/MS/MS) assay. The analyte ciprofloxacin and its internal standard enrofloxacin were extracted from a 100 µL aliquot of monkey serum via solid phase extraction. The extracted samples were injected into a liquid chromatograph equipped with an Agilent Zorbax, 3.5 µm, SB-C8, 4.6 x 75 mm column. The mobile phase was 50% acetonitrile; 50% 10 mM ammonium acetate + formic acid, pH 2.5. The detection method used was mass spectrometry/mass spectrometry. Peak areas of the m/z 332.1 → 288.3 ion transition of ciprofloxacin
L2657: were measured against the m/z 360.2 \to 316.2 ion transition of the internal standard. The calibration range for the assay was from 10 to 5000 ng/mL.
L2658: **MO comment:** Please refer to Microbiology Review for assessment of the assay methods that were employed in this study. The most critical assay in this study was the screening PA, as a positive PA screen was the trigger for treatment. Bacteremia as defined by culture is considered the gold standard. The PA screen, the quantitative PA test, the anti-PA antibody test, and the TNA assay are all exploratory tests being used in this study. It will be important to validate the performance characteristics of these studies.
L2659: ## Statistical Methods:
L2660: The sponsor stated that this study design provided approximately 85% power at a 5% overall significance level to detect an absolute improvement of 56% or more survival at Day 28 post challenge in the ciprofloxacin/raxibacumab combination group. The sample size calculation assumed an 8.3% (1 of 12) survival at Day 28 in the placebo group and a 64.3% (9 of 14) survival at Day 28 in the ciprofloxacin /raxibacumab combination group.
L2661: Analyses of the primary and secondary efficacy endpoints was to be performed on the intention-to-treat (ITT) population defined as all animals that were randomized and challenged with *B. anthracis*. The ITT analysis was to be based on the treatment group planned at randomization rather than the actual treatment the animals received. Animals that were spore-challenged, but died before receiving placebo or active treatment, were to be included in this population as treatment failures. All statistical tests were to be 2-sided and performed at a significance level of 0.05.
L2662: The modified ITT (MITT) population was defined as a subset of the ITT population that included all animals that received a study agent. The MITT analysis was to be based on the planned treatment group rather than the actual treatment received. The as-treated population was defined as the set of all animals that received a study agent with the assignment to treatment group that was based on the actual treatment administered to the subjects. The as-treated analysis was to be based on the actual treatment that the animals received.
L2663: **MO comment:** Please refer to Statistical review by Lan Zeng, Ph. D. In communication with the Sponsor, FDA indicated that the per protocol population (those that were bacteremic at the time of treatment) would be the study population of interest for efficacy analysis.
L2664: ## Endpoints:
L2665: ## Primary Efficacy Endpoint:
L2666: The primary efficacy endpoint was survival at Day 28 in the ITT population. Animals that were spore-challenged, but died before receiving placebo or any
L2667: active treatment, were included in this population as treatment failures. The primary analysis of the primary efficacy endpoint was to compare the percent of animals alive at study Day 28 post challenge between the placebo group (Group 1) and the ciprofloxacin/raxibacumab group (Group 3). The comparison was performed using the 2-sided Fisher's exact test.
L2668: As an exploratory analysis of the primary efficacy endpoint, the point estimate with a 95% confidence interval (CI) was presented for the difference in the survival at Day 28 between the ciprofloxacin group (Group 2) and the ciprofloxacin/raxibacumab combination group (Group 3).
L2669: As a sensitivity analysis of the primary efficacy endpoint, the percent of animals alive at study Day 28 post challenge between the placebo group (Group 1) and the ciprofloxacin/raxibacumab combination group (Group 3) was to be compared via the 2 sided Fisher's exact test in the as-treated population, the modified ITT population, and the population of all animals that were randomized, including those that were randomized but not challenged with *B. anthracis*. The same sensitivity analyses was to be performed for the point estimate and 95% CI of the difference in the survival at Day 28 between the ciprofloxacin group (Group 2) and the ciprofloxacin/raxibacumab combination group (Group 3). The percent of animals alive at Day 28 post challenge between the placebo group (Group 1) and the ciprofloxacin/raxibacumab combination group (Group 3) was to be compared in (but not limited to) the following subgroups via 2-sided Fisher's exact test if the sample size was large enough: Monkeys that were confirmed to be toxicemic at the time of treatment initiation, monkeys that were confirmed to be bacteremic at the time of treatment initiation, monkeys that were confirmed to be toxicemic and bacteremic at the time of treatment initiation, and monkeys that were confirmed to be toxicemic and/or bacteremic at the time of treatment initiation. In addition, the point estimate of the difference in the survival at Day 28 between the ciprofloxacin group (Group 2) and the ciprofloxacin/raxibacumab combination group (Group 3) was to be presented with a 95% CI in each of the above subgroups. Subgroup analyses were not to be subject to multiple comparison adjustment.
L2670: **MO comment:** This study report has been submitted in support of the licensing application for the treatment of inhalational anthrax in humans under the Animal Rule so it is important to ensure that the study population in nonhuman primates is sufficiently reflective of the potential human population with anthrax disease. Therefore, the efficacy assessments in this study will focus on the outcome in the per protocol population of animals that were bacteremic at the time of treatment. The outcomes in the ITT and the modified ITT populations should trend in the same direction as the outcomes in the per protocol population.
L2671: ## Secondary Efficacy Endpoint:
L2672: The secondary efficacy endpoint was survival time from spore challenge to death or to the end of the study period. Analyses of the secondary efficacy endpoint were to be performed on the ITT population. For animals that were alive at the end of the 28-day post challenge period, survival times were to be censored on the date of study completion. The log-rank test was to be used to compare the animals' survival time between the placebo group (Group 1) and each of the treatment groups. The survival time was also to be compared between the ciprofloxacin group (Group 2) and the ciprofloxacin/raxibacumab combination group (Group 3) using the same method. The analysis of the secondary efficacy endpoint was not to be subject to multiple comparison adjustment.
L2673: Exploratory analyses were to be conducted to explore the associations between monkeys' survival at Day 28 with the inhaled dose exposure to *B. anthracis* spores, time to onset of symptoms, time to detectable serum PA levels, and time to onset of bacteremia. Additional analyses were to be conducted to explore the immune response generated following anthrax spore challenge by comparing the seroconversion from baseline in anti-PA antibodies and TNA among surviving monkeys in each group. If data were available, additional subgroup analysis of the primary efficacy endpoint were to be conducted for monkeys confirmed to be anti-PA antibody negative at baseline.
L2674: ## Statistical Methods for Ciprofloxacin and Raxibacumab PK, and Serum PA Kinetics
L2675: Serum ciprofloxacin concentration-time data, serum raxibacumab concentration-time data, serum PA concentration-time data, individual ciprofloxacin PK parameters, individual raxibacumab PK parameters, individual PA kinetic parameters, serum anti-PA antibody concentrations, and serum TNA titers were summarized using descriptive statistics (number of observations [N], mean, standard deviation [SD], standard error [SE], coefficient of variation [CV%], minimum, median, maximum, geometric mean, and 95% CI). Unpaired t-tests were used to compare ciprofloxacin Cmax,1 and Cmax,n between Groups 2 and 3. For animals that survived, an unpaired t-test was used to compare PA t1/2 between Group 2 and Group 3. Unpaired t-tests were used to compare serum anti-PA antibody or TNA concentrations at corresponding collection times between Group 2 and Group 3. All comparisons were carried out at the \alpha = 0.05 level of significance.
L2676: **MO comment:** Please refer to the Clinical Pharmacology Review for PK analysis.
L2677: ## PROTOCOL CHANGES:
L2678: The original protocol was dated February 18, 2008. Four amendments were issued. Amendment 1 was issued prior to challenge, amendment 2 was issued
L2679: post-challenge, and amendments 3 and 4 were issued after the in-life phase of the study.
L2680: - Amendment 1 – March 17, 2008The credentials for the Safety and Health Officer for the study were incorrect in the original protocol and were corrected.
- The dose of sterile WFI used for the ciprofloxacin control was changed from 2 mL/kg to 7.5 mL in the 1st footnote of the study design table. This was done to ensure that all groups received comparable treatments.
- The blood collection schedule (Table 2) was updated to specify that blood collected in SST tubes for ciprofloxacin analysis would not be chilled or placed on ice packs after collection. The requirement was changed as such because the flow properties of the gel barriers in the SST tubes used is temperature-dependent; therefore gel flow could be impeded if these tubes were chilled or placed on ice packs. In addition, this amendment specified that a single 2 mL SST tube may be used to collect blood at the required timepoints rather than two 1 mL tubes.
- The protocol was amended to specify that all serum samples to be shipped to HGS for analysis of raxibacumab, PA, anti-PA and/or TNA would be divided into 2 aliquots of approximately the same volume prior to shipment. This was done to reduce the number of freeze/thaw cycles for backup samples, thus reducing the chance that sample integrity might be compromised. The wording in Section 6.11 (Ciprofloxacin [PK] assay) of the protocol was also adjusted to reflect this change.
- Per FDA request, a statement was added to the end of Section 6.14 (Necropsy and Histopathology) to specify that the study pathologist was to be blinded to the treatment group assignment until all necropsy and histopathology study activities had been completed.
- The Statistical Methods section of the protocol was updated to include all of the statistical methods included in the analytical plan submitted by HGS to FDA.
- Amendment 2 – March 25, 2008Wording in Section 8.4 (Dose Confirmation) was changed to specify that Cipro® IV, 10 mg/mL was to be used on study rather than ciprofloxacin oral solution (which was not commercially available).
- Section 6.9 (Raxibacumab Assay) was changed to clarify that raxibacumab PK analysis would not be performed on all samples collected as indicated in Table 2; the “X” in the table indicates that a serum sample was to be collected, processed, and shipped to HGS for testing.
L2681: - Per FDA request, a statement was added to the end of Section 6.6 (Bacteremia [Culture]) indicating that the technicians preparing the bacteremia cultures would be blinded to the treatment assignments for the duration of the study.
- Amendment 3 – July 3, 2008Section 6.2 (Aerosol Challenge) was corrected to specify that the targeted inhaled *B anthracis* dose of 200 x LD50 was 1.24 x 107 spores rather than 2.47 x 107 spores per animal as was incorrectly stated in the original protocol.
- Section 6.15 (Challenge Survivors) was corrected to specify that monkeys surviving the 30-day post-treatment period will receive exit physical examinations and TB tests prior to leaving the BL-3 facility, and that blood samples will be collected for use in assay development.
- Section 11.0 (Biosafety Considerations) was corrected to clarify that the entire 60-day post-study observation period would not be conducted under BL-2 conditions.
- Amendment 4 – November 10, 200Section 3.0 (Location of Testing Facilities) was corrected to specify that PK and kinetic analyses were conducted at FSC.
- Section 6.14 (Necropsy and Histopathology) was corrected to specify that histopathology will be performed on all animals that died on study.

L2748: ## Other Parameters Measured:
L2749: The majority of animals exhibited clinical signs consistent with anthrax following the spore challenge. The most common clinical features were lethargy, not eating, and respiratory abnormalities.
L2750: The MIC results confirmed that bacteria cultured from the blood of challenged animals were inhibited by similar concentrations of levofloxacin and ciprofloxacin as was the challenge material.
L2751: Body temperature was monitored in all animals. An elevation in body temperature or loss of diurnal rhythm was apparent at 1 to 4 days post-challenge. The trends observed suggest that the animals were presenting non-specific signs of illness similar to results documented during previous animal therapeutic studies. Body weights were not collected after day 0.
L2752: CRP levels were relatively consistent prior to challenge and prior to treatment. For most of the animals, CRP levels increased and peaked between 24-72 hours post-treatment. A majority of the monkeys that survived showed low CRP levels
L2753: at 14 days post challenge. Placebo-treated monkeys (all non-survivors) had elevations in CRP prior to death.
L2754: Positive blood cultures were documented in all the placebo animals at some point post-challenge (2 were not bacteremic at the time of treatment). One animal in each of the two treatment groups was not bacteremic at the time of treatment. Those animals were never bacteremic and they both survived.
L2755: Anti-PA antibodies were collected pre-dose and at 21 and 28 days following treatment for surviving animals. The data are presented in Table 8. There were no statistically significant differences in mean serum anti-PA antibody concentrations between the 2 treatment groups, indicating that co-administration of raxibacumab with ciprofloxacin did not affect the formation of anti-PA antibodies by the surviving monkeys, relative to ciprofloxacin alone.

L2759: Serum TNA titers were drawn for all surviving animals predose and at days 21 and 28 for all surviving animals, and the data are presented in Table 9. The mean serum TNA titers for the ciprofloxacin alone dose group were significantly higher (about 2-fold) than those for the ciprofloxacin plus raxibacumab dose group. It should be noted that these differences were not reflected in altered survival between the 2 groups, suggesting that the TNA response in monkeys administered both ciprofloxacin and raxibacumab was adequate for survival.

L2763: Serum PA concentrations were not measurable in the specimen collected about 7 days prior to the spore challenge for three monkeys. The exceptions were C31014 (ciprofloxacin/raxibacumab treatment group, at 3.76 ng/mL) and C23088 and C25576 in the control group, with prechallenge concentrations of 0.94 and 3.39 ng/mL, respectively. According to the sponsor, PA values rose sharply just prior to 40 hours post challenge. Among some placebo-treated non-survivors, PA values exhibited a brief plateau during the period from 40 to 80 hours post challenge, which was generally followed by a 2nd rise in PA levels that lasted until death. There was no plateau among ciprofloxacin/raxibacumab-treated non-survivors, and PA levels declined through time of death; for 1 of these animals (C31142) the decline was followed by a rise in PA just prior to death. Among ciprofloxacin and ciprofloxacin/raxibacumab-treated survivors, the 2nd rise in PA did not occur; rather, the PA declined to undetectable levels for the majority of monkeys by the end of the study.
L2764: **MO comment:** While there were some increases in temperature noted in the monkeys, this was not used as a trigger for treatment in the monkeys in this study. While some trends in CRP data were noted, this was not used as a trigger for treatment or a predictive factor in this study.
L2765: There was no statistically significant difference between anti-PA levels in animals treated with ciprofloxacin alone or with the ciprofloxacin/raxibacumab combination. It is interesting to note that the anti-PA levels were higher in the primary efficacy trial compared with the values seen in this combination trial (775\mug/mL in the primary efficacy trial raxibacumab group vs. 100\mug/mL in animals that received raxibacumab in the combination trial).
L2766: Serum TNA titers were higher in the ciprofloxacin only treated animals. Of note, TNA titers in the animals that received raxibacumab in this combination study were markedly lower (3400) than levels seen with the same dose of raxibacumab in the pivotal trial (14,827).
L2767: Please see the Microbiology review for a discussion of the PA assays. PA values appear to demonstrate inter-animal variability. It is not clear why 3 animals had detectable levels of PA prior to challenge.
L2768: ## Safety Results
L2769: Limited safety information was provided during this study. Gross pathology and histopathology were available on those animals that died.
L2770: The sponsor notes that although there was a general trend of increasing WBC counts following challenge in all animals, a more rapid rise in WBC was generally noted in the placebo group and a comparatively stable pattern among active
L2771: treatment group survivors. Following treatment, WBC counts continued to rise through Day 8 post challenge. Elevated counts were observed in all groups post-treatment. Surviving animals demonstrated normalization of their WBC by 2-3 weeks post challenge.
L2772: The sponsor noted that following treatment, platelet levels dropped consistently in placebo-treated monkeys until death. Monkeys in both active treatment groups had a decrease in platelet counts through 72 hours post-treatment followed by increases by 8 days post challenge.
L2773: The sponsor noted that RBC levels for the vast majority of monkeys decreased following spore challenge. RBCs in placebo-treated monkeys trended negative until their death, while in the majority of monkeys in both active treatment groups, the RBC counts stabilized and trended positive through the end of the study.
L2774: Profiles for neutrophil and lymphocyte counts were similar to those seen for the WBCs.
L2775: **MO comment:** The hematology data are most suggestive of a non-specific process associated with the acute anthrax infection in these animals, as was seen in the pivotal efficacy trial in the cynomolgus monkeys. Of note, in this study, there was no increase in the number of basophils seen after challenge, as had been seen in the pivotal efficacy trial in the cynomolgus monkeys.
L2776: ## Necropsy and Histopathology:
L2777: In brief, gross lesions at necropsy consistent with anthrax included adrenal gland discoloration (indicating the presence of bacteria); brain/meningeal red-stained accumulation, discoloration or foci (hemorrhage and inflammation); abdominal and/or thoracic cavity fluid (effusion); enlargement of axillary, bronchial, mandibular and/or mediastinal lymph nodes (edema, fibrin exudation, and hemorrhage); and skin or thymic fluid (edema). Gross lesions unrelated to anthrax were liver foci in C24781 in the placebo group (metazoan parasites), lung discoloration in C24791 in the ciprofloxacin/raxibacumab group (pneumonia related to gavage error), and a tan lesion in the inguinal skin of C30988 in the ciprofloxacin group (chronic cellulitis and myositis). Pathology results for C24791 (ciprofloxacin/raxibacumab group) was consistent with fibrinosuppurative bronchopneumonia related to gavage error, as no *B. anthracis* organisms were evident in any tissue according to the sponsor. The large tan lesion in the left inguinal region of animal C30988 (ciprofloxacin group), which led to euthanasia, was consistent with chronic inflammation in the subcutis and muscle with thrombosis of regional arteries. It is possible that arterial thrombosis was the primary lesion, with inflammation, tissue degeneration and fibrosis occurring secondary to hypoxia and trauma to the area by the animal. While the initial insult cannot be determined, this lesion is not likely related to anthrax, as no anthrax bacteria were present in any tissue.
L2778: Microscopic findings consistent with anthrax were present in 13/15 animals examined histologically. Lesions typical of anthrax in this study included brain hemorrhage and meningitis; tubular degeneration in the kidney; liver necrosis and sinusoidal leukocytosis; edema, fibrin exudation, hemorrhage, neutrophilic inflammation, and lymphocyte necrosis affecting the spleen, thymus, lung and multiple lymph nodes; and the presence of large rodshaped bacteria consistent with *B. anthracis* in many of the organs evaluated histologically.
L2779: The only antibiotic-treated monkey to die with lesions of anthrax was animal C31142 (ciprofloxacin/raxibacumab group). This animal had the most severe brain lesions of all animals evaluated histologically but had fewer lesions and bacteria in other organs. Notably, time to death for this animal was 10 days, which was more than the time to death for any of the placebo-treated animals with brain lesions.
L2780: **MO comment:** The histopathology observed in the animals that died in this study is consistent with anthrax. Animal C24791 had evidence of death due to bronchopneumonia from a gavage error. The animal was not bacteremic at the time of death but the mediastinal lymph node showed 1-5 colonies on primary streak but contamination was noted. The bronchial lymph node was enlarged and mottled. No bacteria were noted in any tissues on histopathology.
L2781: In the 12 placebo treated animals, 8 had no gross and no to level 1 bacteria with an average time to death of 99.1 hours. Two of the placebo animals had meningeal congestion and level 1 bacteria with an average survival time of 103.6 hours. One of the placebo animals had discolored meninges, hemorrhage, and level 2 bacteria with a survival time of 100 hours, and one placebo animal had hemorrhagic meningitis with level 3 bacteria, hemorrhage and meningitis and a survival time of 128.5 hours. In summary, 11 of the 12 placebo animals had a low level of pathology (as defined in the pivotal efficacy trial in cynomolgus monkeys) and one animal had a high level of pathology. It is interesting to note that the animal with the high level of pathology inadvertently received a dose of ciprofloxacin.
L2782: Only one treated animal in the ciprofloxacin/raxibacumab group died of anthrax disease. That animal had evidence of hemorrhagic meningitis that affected the entire brain with level 3 bacteria, level 1 hemorrhage, and level 3 meningitis. That animal survived 238.7 hours.
L2783: There was no report of any neurologic sequelae in any of the surviving animals, but it is not known how they were evaluated.
L2784: ## STUDY 789-G923702 CONCLUSIONS
L2785: This was a parallel-group, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled GLP study in 40 healthy male and female cynomolgus monkeys to evaluate the efficacy of
L2786: raxibacumab in combination with ciprofloxacin as a therapeutic treatment in cynomolgus monkeys with inhalation anthrax
L2787: ## **Efficacy conclusions:**
L2788: - Both the ciprofloxacin treated group and the ciprofloxacin/raxibacumab treated group showed statistically significant superiority over placebo in both the sponsor's ITT analysis and the FDA primary analysis.
- For the FDA primary analysis the survival rate in the placebo group was 0%, the survival rate in the ciprofloxacin treated group was 100% and the survival rate in the ciprofloxacin/raxibacumab treated group was 84.6 percent. The treated groups were superior to placebo (p&lt;0.0001).
- There was no differences in survival rates between the two treated groups.
L2789: ## **Safety conclusions:**
L2790: - Safety data were limited in the study to findings on gross necropsy, histopathology, and serial CBCs.
- In the placebo animals, 11 animals had evidence of low CNS pathology while 1 animal had high CNS pathology. That animal inadvertently was exposed to ciprofloxacin. Only one treated animal died of anthrax disease and that animal had evidence of hemorrhagic meningitis that affected the entire brain. No surviving animals were sacrificed.
- Based on the available analyses, the pathophysiologic basis for the increased CNS inflammation seen in the pivotal efficacy trial in cynomolgus monkeys is not clear. The number of animals analyzed is small. While it is reassuring that no gross neurologic findings were seen in the surviving animals, and no brain abnormalities were seen in toxicologic studies, a potential interaction between anthrax and raxibacumab contributing to CNS inflammation and hemorrhage cannot be ruled out. It will be important to examine the histopathology in animals that die in any subsequent studies and it would be reassuring to examine the brains of those animals that survive in order to establish normal brain histology in survivors. If it is not possible to sacrifice survivors, then more formal neurologic assessments including imaging studies should be performed in subsequent studies.

L2794: ## Nonclinical Study Report 724-G005829: Evaluation of Raxibacumab Efficacy as Therapeutic Treatment Against Inhalation Anthrax in the Cynomolgus Macaque
L2795: **PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATOR:** Jason M. Mott, DVM, Ph.D.
L2796: **STUDY CENTER:** Battelle Biomedical Research Center (BBRC)
L2797: **STUDY PERIOD:** September 15, 2007 to January 11, 2008
L2798: **REPORT DATE:** April 26, 2008
L2799: **STUDY PROCEDURE:** Study was conducted under GLP
L2800: ## **OBJECTIVES:**
L2801: ## **Primary Objective:**
L2802: To evaluate the efficacy of raxibacumab when administered as a therapeutic treatment against lethality due to inhalation exposure to *B. anthracis* in cynomolgus monkeys
L2803: ## **Additional Objectives:**
L2804: To determine the PK of raxibacumab following a single IV raxibacumab dose and the kinetics of *B. anthracis* PA in monkeys with inhalation anthrax
L2805: **METHODOLOGY:** Parallel-group, double-blind, randomized, placebo controlled GLP study in healthy male and female cynomolgus monkeys to evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of a single IV dose of raxibacumab in anthrax spore inhalation-challenged monkeys experiencing symptoms of inhalation anthrax
L2806: **NUMBER OF ANIMALS:** 40 naïve cynomolgus monkeys were randomized into 2 separate treatment groups of 14 animals and a placebo group of 12 monkeys (each 50% male and 50% female). Two animals were held as replacements but were not used.
L2807: **STUDY DRUG:** Upon detection of serum PA via the screening assay, IV raxibacumab was given as a single bolus infusion at either a 20 or 40 mg/kg dose.
L2808: Raxibacumab, is a recombinant, fully human IgG1 mAb that binds *B. anthracis* PA with high affinity and inhibits its biological activity. Raxibacumab is expressed in the NS0 mouse myeloma cell line and secreted into culture media, from which it is purified by a series of chromatography and filtration steps.
L2809: Raxibacumab was supplied by the sponsor as a sterile liquid formulation (50 mg/mL) in a formulation buffer consisting of 0.13 mg/mL citric acid, 2.8 mg/mL sodium citrate, 10 mg/mL sucrose, 18 mg/mL glycine, 0.2mg/mL polysorbate 80, pH 6.5. Storage was at 2-8°C.
L2810: Raxibacumab used for the two treatment groups came from lot #71044, manufactured on October 13, 2006. The placebo buffer came from lot #71043, manufactured on October 4, 2006.
L2811: **MO comment:** There was no documentation of the actual product used for this study (M10 vs. M11). Subsequent to the study report submission, HGS confirmed that M11 was the product used for this study.
L2812: All monkeys received a single IM dose of diphenhydramine (1 mg/mL) within 5 minutes prior to study agent administration.
L2813: **DURATION OF TREATMENT:** Raxibacumab or placebo was to be administered IV immediately to each individual animal following detection of serum PA via the PA screening assay. Within 5 minutes prior to treatment each monkey was to receive a single 1 mg/kg IM dose of diphenhydramine.
L2814: **TREATMENT COMPLIANCE:** Study drug infusion information, including dosage and volume prescribed, and volume administered, was recorded.
L2815: **STUDY DESIGN:** This was a parallel-group, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled GLP study in healthy male and female cynomolgus monkeys to evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of a single IV dose of raxibacumab in anthrax spore inhalation-challenged monkeys experiencing symptoms of inhalation anthrax. Forty naïve cynomolgus monkeys were to be randomized into 3 separate groups, two groups of 14 monkeys and 1 group of 12 monkeys (each group 50% male, 50% female).
L2816: Monkeys were to be randomized to 1 of 3 aerosol challenge days and randomized to a challenge order each day. On Study Day 0, monkeys were to be challenged with a targeted 200 x lethal dose (LD_{50}) (1.24 \times 10^7 spores) of *B. anthracis* spores (Ames strain) by a Collison nebulizer and delivered using a head-only inhalation exposure chamber. When an animal exhibited a positive serum PA level via the screening assay or at 54 hours post challenge, a single bolus IV injection of either 40 or 20 mg/kg of raxibacumab, or 1 mL/kg of raxibacumab buffer (dependent upon that animal's treatment assignment) was to be administered. Just prior to treatment intervention (within 5 minutes), monkeys were administered a single 1 mg/kg dose of diphenhydramine (or equivalent) intramuscularly (IM).
L2817: ## BACKGROUND:
L2818: Raxibacumab is a fully human monoclonal antibody (mAb) antitoxin that specifically binds protective antigen (PA), preventing the association of PA with the anthrax toxin receptor. The indication currently being sought is the therapeutic treatment of inhalation anthrax. It is hypothesized that raxibacumab could provide benefit following exposure to bioengineered, antibiotic-resistant strains *B. anthracis*.
L2819: Based on the *in vitro* inhibition of PA-mediated cytotoxicity by raxibacumab, HGS performed a number of *in vivo* studies in animal models of anthrax-induced lethality. These studies included pre- and post-exposure prophylaxis studies in Fisher 344 rats injected with lethal toxin, and anthrax spore inhalation studies in New Zealand white rabbits and cynomolgus monkeys.
L2820: ## Rat Studies:
L2821: In the rat model, raxibacumab provided protection against lethality when administered by subcutaneous, IM, or IV routes. A single administration protected the rats for a duration of three weeks. The continuous infusion lethal toxin rat model showed that treatment of symptomatic rats with raxibacumab as
L2822: late as 12 hours after initiation of lethal toxin resulted in improved hemodynamic effects and survival.

- None of the SC animals

- 100% survival if monoclonal given 2 or 3

L2832: ## Rabbit Studies:
L2833: In the NZW rabbits, 100% survival was seen when 40 mg/kg of raxibacumab was given within 12 hours of challenge. When raxibacumab was given prior to challenge, there was a dose response with 40 mg/kg producing 100% survival. Survival decreased when raxibacumab was given 24 and 36 hours following aerosol challenge with only 33% survival in the 40 mg/kg group when given at 24 hours post challenge and 0% survival when the monoclonal (20 mg/kg) was given at 36 hours after challenge. In a treatment study, when the treatment was initiated when the animals had persistent fever or PA positivity, 5/18 in the 20 mg/kg group and 8/18 in the 40 mg/kg group survived.

- Monoclonal administered SC at 1, 5, 10, 20 mg/kg two days prior to challenge
- Monoclonal administered IV at 40 mg/kg immediately after spore challenge

L2844: ## NHP Studies:
L2845: A pre-exposure prophylaxis spore challenge study was done in cynomolgus monkeys. Raxibacumab at doses of 10, 20 and 40 mg/kg were given 2 days prior to aerosol challenge. Survival was 0%, 60%, 70% and 90% in the placebo, 10 mg/kg, 20 mg/kg, and 40 mg/kg doses respectively. Median survival time was longer in all raxibacumab treated groups. Those animals that survived were re-
L2846: challenged (Study 374-N006090) approximately 11 months after the first study. All control animals (6) died while the 21 animals that were re-challenged all survived.

L2848: ## Survival Curves for Cynomolgus Monkeys
## (Adapted from HGS' BLA submission)
L2849: A natural history study was done in the cynomolgus monkey (study # 685-G005762). Eight animals were studied. They received a mean aerosol challenge of 260 \times LD_{50}. Six of eight monkeys died and neither survival or survival time were correlated with challenge dose. The median time to develop bacteremia by culture was 36 hours. The earliest time to death was 85 hours and the latest time to death of those who died was 156 hours. Survival time was correlated with time of PA detection indicating that PA was a predictor of ensuing death. In monkeys and rabbits, the serum PA concentrations rise, plateau, and rise again in those who die but the timing and the magnitude of these changes differ between the species.
L2850: **MO comment:** The information in this background section has been culled from submitted study reports and annual reports. There has been no official review of these studies and these summary data may need to be revised after such review has occurred.
L2851: ## STUDY 724-G005829 PROTOCOL
L2852: ## Design:
L2853: This was a parallel-group, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled GLP study in healthy male and female cynomolgus monkeys to evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of a single IV dose of raxibacumab in anthrax spore inhalation challenged monkeys experiencing the symptoms of inhalation anthrax.
L2854: ## Inclusion criteria:
L2855: - Male and female juvenile (&lt; 5 years of age) naïve Chinese colony bred cynomolgus monkeys by (b) (4).
- Weight 2.5 to 4.5 kg at randomization.
- Free of malformations and clinical signs of disease.
- Monkeys were to be tested and verified negative for tuberculosis and screened within 30 days prior to receipt at Battelle and found to be negative for Simian Immunodeficiency Virus, Simian T-Lymphotrophic Virus-1 (STLV-1), and *Cercopithecine herpesvirus* 1 (Herpes B virus). All monkeys were required to be tested negative for Simian Retrovirus (SRV1 and SRV2), anti-PA reactive antibodies, and circulating PA prior to randomization.
L2856: ## Exclusion criteria:
L2857: - Malformations.
- Clinical signs and symptoms of disease.
- Any monkeys outside the specified weight range.
- Any monkey with any one of the infections listed above.
L2858: ## Euthanasia Criteria:
L2859: Any of the following criteria prompted immediate euthanasia:
L2860: - Presence of any seizure denoting primary central nervous system disease.
- Respiratory distress, dyspnea, or forced abdominal respirations.
- Unresponsive to touch or external stimuli.
- Moribundity.
L2861: Euthanasia was warranted when all the clinical signs below were observed:
L2862: - Recumbence and weakness.
- Progressive state of depression.
- \ge 20\% body weight loss.
- Body temperature below 97°F; indicative of shock.
- Total anorexia with duration longer than 48 hours.
L2863: **MO comment:** In amendment 1 of the protocol, the FDA requested more frequent observations of the monkeys. Without this recommended increase in observation frequency, it is likely that more animals would have been found
L2864: dead. Observations were required every 6 hours starting 24 hours after challenge to minimize the chance that animals would be found dead. On inspection of the records, there are no clear violations of the euthanasia criteria. Despite these criteria, 11 of the 24 animals who died were found dead.
L2865: ## Aerosol Challenge:
L2866: Monkeys were randomized by sex to study group and randomized to one of three challenge days. The monkeys were then assigned a random challenge order within the challenge day using random numbers generated by the SAS® RANUNI function. Animals were challenged via the inhalation route with *B. anthracis* (Ames strain). On the day of challenge, monkeys were anesthetized with Telazol and placed into a plethysmography chamber within a Class III cabinet system where they were challenged with a targeted dose of 200 x LD50 using a Collison nebulizer and delivered via a head-only inhalation exposure chamber.
L2867: ## Randomization of Monkeys:
L2868: A tattoo was used to identify each animal. Following telemetry transmitter implantation, the monkeys were allowed to recover until approximately 10-14 days prior to challenge when they were transferred into the BL-3 facility. Monkeys were identified by individual cage cards that stated tattoo number, study number, study director, and sex of the monkey. Forty-two cynomolgus monkeys were available for the study (20 females and 22 males) and 40 (20 females and 20 males) were randomly selected to be placed on study utilizing random numbers generated by the SAS® RANUNI function. The two replacement animals were not used. The 40 monkeys were to be randomized by sex to one group of 12 animals, and 2 groups of 14 animals (all three groups with equal numbers of males and females) and aerosol challenge day utilizing the SAS® PLAN procedure. The monkeys were assigned a randomized challenge order within aerosol challenge day utilizing random numbers generated by the SAS® RANUNI function.
L2869: ## Treatments and Study Groups:
L2870: Cynomolgus monkeys were randomized to one of three aerosol challenge days and a challenge order per day. On day 0, monkeys were challenged with a targeted aerosol dose of 200 x LD50 spores of *B. anthracis* (Ames strain). When an animal had a positive serum PA level via screening assay or at 54 hours post-challenge, a single bolus IV injection of 40 mg/kg raxibacumab, 20 mg/kg raxibacumab, or 1 mL/kg raxibacumab buffer was administered. Just prior to treatment intervention, all monkeys were administered a single 1 mg/kg IM dose of diphenhydramine. Treatment groups are defined in Table 1.
L2871: Number of Monkeys Planned	Dose	Route/Frequency	Treatment Point
Group 1	14	40 mg/kg raxibacumab (1 mL/kg)	IV/single dose	Individual treatment times based on serum PA levels
Group 2	14	20 mg/kg raxibacumab (1 mL/kg)	IV/single dose	Individual treatment times based on serum PA levels
Group 3 (placebo)	12	Raxibacumab buffer (1mL/kg)	IV/single dose	Individual treatment times based on serum PA levels

L2873: **Table 1 Treatment Group Designation**
L2874: ## **Blinding:**
L2875: Staff administering study agent to and/or conducting assessments of study monkeys post challenge were to be blinded to their treatment assignments in order to preclude the introduction of bias into the study. Dilutions of the study agents were to be sealed in sterile dosing vials labeled X, Y, or Z. Dilutions were to be performed no earlier than 3 days prior to challenge and were stored at 2-8°C prior to dosing. Documentation of vial content was to be controlled by Battelle's Quality Assurance Unit until 32 days post-challenge of the final challenge cohort. All animals were to receive 1mL/kg of study agent to maintain blinding of treatment assignment.
L2876: ## **Study Agent Administration:**
L2877: Raxibacumab or placebo were to be administered IV via a single bolus injection upon detection of positive serum PA via screening assay.
L2878: **MO comment:** The treatment in the monkeys was administered as a bolus injection. In human studies, raxibacumab is to be administered by infusion over 2.5 hours. This difference in administration times needs to be taken into account in matching the animal and human PK parameters, especially related to Cmax.
L2879: ## **Clinical Observations:**
L2880: All monkeys were to be observed every 6 hours beginning 24 hours post median challenge time and ending 192 hours (8 days) post median challenge time. Animals were observed for clinical signs including, but not limited to, anorexia, lethargy, respiratory distress, moribundity, activity (recumbent, weak, or unresponsive), seizures, and other clinical observations (noted by the observer). Appetite was monitored twice a day during this period. In the pre-challenge period and from days 9 through 28 post-challenge, animals were observed twice daily. In order to limit the number of animals that were found dead, animals documented as having respiratory distress or being unresponsive may have had
L2881: more frequent observations performed and telemetry data reviewed to determine if temperature or activity levels were decreasing.
L2882: **MO comment:** It is important to note that despite the observations every 6 hours, 11 of the 24 animals who died were found dead. Respiratory distress was infrequently seen in the animals (labored respirations in 2 and respiratory distress in 1). There is no evidence of more frequent monitoring in any of the animals documented in the clinical observations data. One animal was recorded as being normal in the 6 hours prior to being found dead.
L2883: Body temperatures and activity levels were to be monitored at least hourly beginning 10 to 14 days prior to challenge, and until the end of the in-life animal phase (32 days post challenge). Body temperatures were to be recorded via TA-D70 telemetry transmitters (b) (4) after surgical implantation.
L2884: **MO comment:** Isolated temperature spikes into the high 40's and low 50's were noted for all of the monkeys in the study. HGS postulates that there is the possibility that transmitter frequencies from different animals may have interacted with each other due to the proximity of the monkeys to each other in the cages. The manufacturer suggests that the receivers may be reading the interaction signals and this may result in an additive effect and abnormally high readings can be observed. It is not clear how significant a problem this interference might be. Since temperatures were not used as a trigger for treatment in this study, there was no significance of these spikes in this study.
L2885: ## Necropsy and Histopathology:
L2886: Gross necropsies were to be performed on all monkeys that were found dead or were euthanized. Sections of target tissues including but not limited to brain/meninges, lungs, liver, spleen, kidney and mediastinal lymph nodes as well as all gross lesions were to be preserved in 10% neutral buffered formalin. To confirm death or illness due to anthrax, histopathology was to be performed, as deemed necessary, by a board certified veterinary pathologist. A representative sample of spleen, liver, and mediastinal lymph node was to be homogenized and plated on blood agar plates for qualitative assessment of *B. anthracis*.
L2887: Following the analysis of the initial necropsy data that included histopathology analysis of only the two animals that did not have gross evidence of anthrax disease, the FDA requested that histopathology analysis be performed on all tissues in all animals that died. The reading of the tissues from study 724-G005829 was performed under GLP as Protocol 901-G005829. The draft report of this study was submitted as serial 0088 dated October 31, 2008. The study was read in a blinded manner with the study pathologist only having access to pre-study animal numbers and gross observations during initial microscopic interpretation. Study blinding was removed after all of the slides were read by
L2888: the study pathologist but prior to peer review. The FDA also asked for independent pathology review of the slides. The independent evaluation of the pathology slides was completed by Experimental Pathology Laboratories, Inc. (EPL). The draft report of their results was submitted as serial 0093 on December 23, 2008. At EPL, all the slides were read in a blinded manner and then peer reviewed.

L2890: Blood volumes were taken from a femoral artery or vein, saphenous vein, or other appropriate vein on the days specified in Table 2. Blood volumes were within the guidelines established by the Battelle IACUC. All post-challenge pre-treatment blood samples were to be collected relative to the median challenge time at the time points stated \pm 1 hour. Median challenge time was to be calculated from the challenge end time of the first and last monkeys challenged within a single challenge day. All post-treatment blood collections were to be collected relative to the end time of each animal's IV treatment.
