L2898: ## **Assays:**
L2899: Bacteremia by blood culture was performed at Battelle according to their SOP. Macroscopic observations were performed and colonies were assessed for hemolysis, type, size, color, and morphology. If \gamma-hemolytic, white colonies of 4 to 10 mm in diameter with a rough appearance and irregular edges were present, the sample was documented as positive for *B. anthracis* bacteremia.
L2900: For bacteremia by PCR, genomic DNA was isolated using a QIAGEN DNeasy Kit. Samples were shipped to HGS where PCR amplification was conducted using *B. anthracis* specific primers according to HGS SOPs. The PCR procedure consisted of 3 assays: the 18s PCR assay, the pagA PCR assay, and the chromosomal PCR assay. The 18s assay tests the quality and concentration of genomic DNA, the pagA assay tests for the presence of the *B. anthracis* pX01 DNA plasmid, and the chromosomal assay tests for the presence of *B. anthracis* chromosomal DNA.
L2901: MICs of levofloxacin and ciprofloxacin for *B. anthracis* challenge material, on positive cultures pre-IV treatment, and on positive cultures from terminal blood samples were to be determined.
L2902: Hematology evaluation was performed with the Advia® 120. Hematology slides were to be prepared and reviewed when necessary as determined by a highly-trained hematology technician or the Study Director. Hematology parameters that were monitored were WBC, RBC, hemoglobin, hematocrit, MCV, MCH, MCHC, RDW, platelets, MPV, % and numbers of neutrophils, % and numbers of lymphocytes, % and numbers of monocytes, % and numbers of eosinophils, % and numbers of basophils, neutrophil to lymphocyte % ratio, and neutrophil to lymphocyte number ratio. CRP analysis was to be performed on residual plasma. The CRP analysis was a non-validated assay.
L2903: Serum PA screening assays were performed at Battelle. Undiluted serum samples in triplicate wells were to be incubated in the presence of rabbit anti-PA-biotin and rabbit anti-PA-SULFOTAG for 2 hours at 37°C in a streptavidin-coated assay plate. The limit of detection was established at 1.0 ng/mL based on the qualification experiments. Blood was shipped to HGS for the PA quantitative assay. Total PA (free and raxibacumab-bound) concentrations in serum samples were to be determined using an ECL-based bridging assay using rabbit polyclonal antibody anti-PA-biotin and rabbit pAb anti-PA-SULFO-TAG. The concentrations were interpolated from a reference standard curve. The lower limit of quantification was 0.65 ng/mL.
L2904: Anti-PA antibody concentrations in serum samples were to be determined using an ELISA. Anti-PA antibody was to be captured on wild-type PA coated plates and the concentration was interpolated from a reference standard curve. The lower limit of quantification was &lt; 600 ng/mL.
L2905: TNA titers were to be determined using a cell killing assay in J744A macrophages. Inhibition of PA binding is correlated with increased cell viability. The lower limit of quantification was &lt; 52 titer.
L2906: Serum samples were to be analyzed for raxibacumab using an ECL-based assay where raxibacumab in serum binds to the biotinylated-PA on a streptavidin-coated plate and is detected by the addition of goat anti-human antibody labeled with MSD SULFOTAG. The concentration was interpolated from a reference standard curve. The lower limit of quantification was 940 ng/mL.
L2907: **MO comment:** Please refer to Microbiology Review for assessment of the assay methods that were employed in this study. The most critical assay in this study was the screening PA, as a positive PA screen was the trigger for treatment. Bacteremia as defined by culture is considered the gold standard. The PA screen, the quantitative PA test, the bacteremia by PCR, the anti-PA antibody test, and the TNA assay are all exploratory tests being used in this study. It will be important to validate the performance characteristics of these studies.
L2908: ## Statistical Methods:
L2909: The study design provided 74% power at a 5% significance level to detect an absolute improvement of approximately 49% or more in the 40 mg/kg raxibacumab group assuming an 8.3% survival in the placebo group and a 57.1% survival in the 40 mg/kg raxibacumab group. The primary analysis was performed on the intention-to-treat (ITT) population. All statistical tests were 2-sided and performed at a significance level of 0.05, unless otherwise specified. The primary efficacy analysis was subject to multiple comparison adjustment using a step-down sequential testing procedure. The ITT population was defined as all monkeys that were randomized and challenged with anthrax spores. The modified ITT population was defined as a subset of the ITT population that included all animals that received a study agent based on the planned treatment. The as-treated population was defined as the set of all animals that received a study agent based on the actual treatment.
L2910: **MO comment:** Please refer to Statistical review by Hongling Zhou, Ph. D. In communication with the Sponsor, FDA indicated that the per protocol population (those that were bacteremic at the time of treatment) would be the study population of interest for efficacy analysis.
L2911: ## Endpoints:
L2912: ## Primary Efficacy Endpoint:
L2913: The primary efficacy variable was survival at day 28, defined as the percent of monkeys alive on day 28 in the ITT population. The primary efficacy analysis was performed using a 2-sided likelihood test and was subject to multiple comparison adjustment using a step-down sequential testing procedure:
L2914: - First the 40 mg/kg raxibacumab group was compared with placebo. If this was statistically significant then the 20 mg/kg raxibacumab group was compared with placebo for statistical significance.
L2915: Sensitivity analyses were to be performed for the as-treated population, the modified ITT population, and the group of all animals that were randomized including any that were randomized but not challenged with spores.
L2916: Pre-specified subgroups included monkeys that were confirmed to be bacteremic at the time of treatment and monkeys that were not bacteremic at the time of treatment. If sample size was large enough, subgroups to be evaluated included monkeys toxicemic at the time of treatment, monkeys that were bacteremic and toxicemic at the time of treatment, and monkeys that were bacteremic and/or toxicemic at the time of treatment. These subgroups were identified for events at the time of treatment, events at or before the time of treatment and events at any time. In the subgroup analysis, bacteremic was defined as animals with bacteremia as indicated by culture or PCR assay, and toxicemic was defined as animals with toxemia as indicated by positive PA by quantitative ECL assay.
L2917: **MO comment:** This pivotal study report has been submitted for licensing application for the treatment of inhalational anthrax in humans under the Animal Rule so it is important to ensure that the study population in nonhuman primates is sufficiently reflective of the potential human population with anthrax disease. Therefore, the efficacy assessments in this study will focus on the outcome in the per protocol population of animals that were bacteremic at the time of treatment. The outcomes in the ITT and the modified ITT populations should trend in the same direction as the outcomes in the per protocol population.
L2918: ## Secondary Efficacy Endpoint:
L2919: The secondary efficacy endpoint was survival time, defined as the time from spore challenge to death during the 28 day study period. The Cochran-Armitage test was used to examine the dose response trend in 28-day survival for doses ranging from placebo to 40 mg/kg raxibacumab. The association between survival, inhaled spore dose, time to detectable serum PA and time to onset of bacteremia was to be explored.
L2920: ## Raxibacumab PK
L2921: PK analyses of raxibacumab concentration-time profiles for all raxibacumab-dosed monkeys were conducted using population analysis techniques with NONMEM software. Serum raxibacumab concentration-time data, serum PA concentration-time data, individual raxibacumab PK parameters, individual PA
L2922: kinetic parameters, serum anti-PA antibody concentrations, and serum TNA titers were summarized using descriptive statistics.
L2923: **MO comment:** Please refer to the Clinical Pharmacology Review for PK analysis.
L2924: ## PROTOCOL CHANGES:
L2925: The original protocol was dated July 20, 2007. Four amendments were issued. Amendment 1 was issued prior to randomization, amendment 2 was issued prior to spore challenge, and amendments 3 and 4 consisted of editorial changes.
L2926: - Amendment 1 – August 23, 2007Frequency of clinical observations was increased to every 8 hours during the 8 days following challenge if animals were having respiratory distress or being unresponsive in order to minimize the potential of an animal being found dead. It was also noted that more frequent observations may have induced stress on the other animals.
- In addition to anti-PA antibody analysis, TNA analysis was to be performed on serum samples on day -7 and 30 days post treatment for surviving monkeys.
- Additional detail was included to describe the procedure of blinding Battelle personnel to ensure that the Study Director and all the technicians assessing the animals were adequately blinded to study group assignment.
- Amendment 2 – August 30, 2007An aliquot of test material, control material stock, and dilutions of the test material made for each challenge day were to be shipped to HGS for dose confirmation analysis.
- The day -7 and 30 day post treatment blood collections were deemed unnecessary for the anti-PA antibody quantitative ECL and TNA analysis and were replaced with blood collections on day -3 and 28 days post treatment.
- Amendment 3 – March 25, 2008A description of the secondary efficacy analysis of survival time over 28 days was added to the Analytical and Statistical Plan. This analysis was pre-specified in the Analytical Plan and similar language was added to the protocol for consistency.
- Amendment 4 – April 7, 2008In the Study Design, the heading for quantitative serum PA level incorrectly referred to ELISA and was changed to quantitative ECL assay. Mention of ELISA in subsection 6.8 was also corrected.
L2927: - In section 6.2, the targeted spore dose was incorrectly stated to be 2.47 \times 10^7 spores and was corrected to 1.24 \times 10^7 corresponding to a targeted 200 \times \text{LD}_{50}.

L2940: ## Extent of Anthrax Exposure
L2941: ## Anthrax Exposure Level by Challenge Group
L2942: The mean exposure to *B. anthracis* in the ITT population was 184.0 \pm 46.8 \times \text{LD}_{50} and is summarized in Table 4. Monkeys in the 40 mg/kg raxibacumab group received a lower mean inhaled dose of spores (157 \times \text{LD}_{50}) compared to the placebo group (198 \times \text{LD}_{50}) and the 20 mg/kg raxibacumab group (199 \times \text{LD}_{50}). This finding prompted a sensitivity analysis.
L2943: Three monkeys in the 40 mg/kg raxibacumab group (C23640, C23655, and C24823) were challenged with a dose of spores less than the lowest challenge dose in the placebo group. Excluding those animals did not change the survival benefit (Table 5). The Cox model which included all 40 monkeys showed that, adjusting for the dose of spores, the survival benefit remained statistically significant in the treated groups compared to the placebo group.

L2952: **MO comment:** The spore challenge dose was lower in the 40 mg/kg raxibacumab group than in the other two treatment groups. Dr. Hongling Zhou, statistical reviewer, analyzed the spore challenge doses and confirmed the results in Table 4. There are statistically significant differences in mean spore exposure levels among the three treatment groups (F test, p=0.0255). The p-values (t-test) for further pair-wise comparisons are 0.9413 for the 20 mg/kg raxibacumab group vs. placebo, 0.0123 for the 40 mg/kg raxibacumab group vs. placebo, and 0.0176 for the 20 mg/kg raxibacumab vs. 40 mg/kg raxibacumab groups. The difference in inhaled spores between the 40 mg/kg raxibacumab group and the placebo group is statistically significant even after the conservative Bonferroni multiplicity adjustment. Further examination of the three animals that received the lowest challenge dose revealed that C23640 received the lowest dose at 106.9 x LD50 and died, C24823 received 112 x LD50 and survived, and C23655 received 116 x LD50 and died.
L2953: Dr. Zhou confirmed the sensitivity analysis regarding the exclusion of the three animals with spore exposure less than 120 \times LD_{50}. Dr. Zhou performed additional sensitivity analyses excluding animals with exposure less than 150 \times LD_{50}. For animals that had exposures &gt;150 \times LD_{50}, there were 11 animals in the placebo group, 10 in the 20 mg/kg raxibacumab group, and 9 in the 40 mg/kg raxibacumab group. The fisher's exact test comparing survival rates between the 20 mg/kg raxibacumab group and placebo returned a p-value of 0.0039, and between the 40 mg/kg raxibacumab group and placebo returned a p-value of 0.0005. Statistically significant differences in survival were seen when animals receiving lower spore exposures were excluded.

L2961: In preliminary observations, there was a suggestion that on 9/25/08, there might be a survival difference based on challenge order. Dr. Zhou examined the relationship between survival and the challenge order on 9/25/08. All three monkeys that survived were challenged on or after 11:41 AM. None of the 8 animals who were challenged prior to 11:41 AM survived. The amount of anthrax exposure was slightly lower on average for those who were challenged before 11:41 AM (186.1 \times \text{LD}_{50} before and 202.9 \times \text{LD}_{50} after). The numbers of animals in the subgroups was not sufficient to identify a statistically significant trend of survival for treatment group with respect to challenge order. It is interesting to note that on 9/25/07, there were no early survivors bringing into question whether the spores were hardier during the early part of the challenge. However, no similar findings were seen on the other two challenge days.
L2962: Dr. Zhou also explored the relationship between anthrax exposure level and the probability of survival. The mean dose of spores in those animals that died was compared to the mean dose in those who survived. The 16 animals who survived had a lower mean spore exposure (179 \pm 37.4 \times \text{LD}_{50}) than those who died (187 \pm 52.7 \times \text{LD}_{50}). In the 20 mg/kg raxibacumab group those who survived had an exposure level of 194.8 \pm 42.1 \times \text{LD}_{50} and those that died had an exposure level of 203.2 \pm 64.3 \times \text{LD}_{50}. For the 40 mg/kg raxibacumab group the mean exposure level was higher for those who survived (167.5 \pm 30.5 \times \text{LD}_{50}) than for those who died (138.9 \pm 30 \times \text{LD}_{50}). None of the differences were statistically significant.
L2963: Please see Dr. Hongling Zhou's statistical review for details of these analyses. The study was not powered to detect if differences in challenge doses would lead to differences in survival rates in any of the groups or subgroups.

This might become more important as we try to define a window of opportunity for human treatment.

L3005: ## Other Parameters Measured:
L3006: The majority of animals exhibited clinical signs consistent with anthrax following the spore challenge. The most common clinical features were lethargy, not eating, and respiratory abnormalities.
L3007: The MICs for levofloxacin ranged from 0.5 to 4.0 \mu\text{g/mL} and for ciprofloxacin ranged from 0.25 to 2.0 \mu\text{g/mL}. The MICs confirmed that the bacteria cultured from the blood of aerosol challenged animals was inhibited by similar concentrations of levofloxacin and ciprofloxacin as the original challenge material.
L3008: Body temperature was monitored in all animals. An elevation in body temperature or loss of diurnal rhythm was noted at 2 to 4 days post-challenge and appeared to coincide with decreased activity in the majority of animals. Body weights were not collected after day 0.
L3009: The incidence of positive blood cultures was 100% across all dose groups at some point post-challenge. The positive blood cultures confirm that all monkeys were infected with *B. anthracis*. Five of 40 monkeys did not show bacteremia by PCR prior to treatment. The *pagA* PCR assay was more sensitive than the chromosomal assay for detecting bacterial DNA, as positive samples in the *pagA* assay were detected at earlier time points in 28% of the monkeys. The *pagA* assay data showed correlation with bacteremia by culture at all time points in 75% of the monkeys. In six monkeys, bacteremia was detected by PCR prior to culture while in 4 animals, culture was positive prior to PCR.
L3010: Anti-PA antibodies were collected pre-dose and at 28 days following treatment for surviving animals. The data are presented in Table 11. Values for animals in the 40 mg/kg raxibacumab group are more than 2-fold higher than those in the 20 mg/kg raxibacumab group.

L3018: Serum PA levels were monitored over time in all monkeys. There were no measurable PA levels in specimens collected 3 days prior to challenge. In general, PA values increased sharply just prior to 40 hours post-challenge and reached a plateau between 40 to 80 hours. For non-survivors, the plateau was generally followed by a second spike in PA that increased until death. For survivors, the second spike did not occur and levels declined to undetectable levels for most animals by the end of the study. Higher serum PA levels at the first phase plateau were noted in non-survivors in the 40 mg/kg raxibacumab group compared with placebo animals. The sponsor speculates that this likely reflects the ability of raxibacumab to block the lethal effects of PA so that monkeys with no exposure to raxibacumab died at lower serum PA levels than those who received raxibacumab.
L3019: **MO comment:** Review of the PA screening test, the quantitative PA assay, and the PCR assay is concurrent with this review. Please see the Microbiology review for details.
L3020: While there were some increases in temperature noted in the monkeys, this was not used as a trigger for treatment in the monkeys in this study.
L3021: *There was a significant amount of inter-animal variability in the quantitative PA response. While there was an increase in the first phase plateau noted in the 40 mg/kg raxibacumab group compared with placebo in non-survivors, the range was very broad and the number of animals in the 40 mg/kg raxibacumab group was small.*
L3022: *It is not clear why there was a 2-fold higher level of anti-PA and an almost 3-fold higher level of TNA in the survivors in the 40 mg/kg raxibacumab group compared to the 20 mg/kg raxibacumab group. This will need to be followed in subsequent studies.*
L3023: *For information on raxibacumab PK, please see the Clinical Pharmacology review.*
L3024: ## Safety Results
L3025: Limited safety information was provided during this study. Gross pathology was available on all animals that died with initial histopathology information on 2 animals that did not have gross pathologic evidence of anthrax disease. In addition, serial CBCs and C-reactive protein levels were drawn. Under protocol 901-G005829, Battelle reviewed histopathology of all animals that died and EPL provided independent pathology review of these tissues. None of the surviving animals were reported to have persistent neurologic findings, and neurologic findings were not more common in treated animals that died compared to placebo animals that died.
L3026: WBC levels were stable in all monkeys through 24 hours post spore challenge, spiked and then declined to baseline levels between 24 to 48 hours post-challenge for most monkeys. For non-survivors, this decline was followed by WBC increases until the time of death. For the majority of survivors, WBC levels approached baseline levels for the remainder of the study.
L3027: Platelet counts showed a decline after approximately 24 hours post challenge. In non-survivors platelet counts continued to decline until the time of death. In survivors, the platelet count decline ended approximately at 72 hours and was followed by an upward trend through the end of the study.
L3028: RBC levels began to decline in all animals through 24 hours post-challenge. In non-survivors, the decline continued until death. In survivors, the RBC levels started to trend in a positive direction approximately 168 hours post-challenge.
L3029: Serial WBC differentials were recorded for all animals. The neutrophil percent increased following challenge but then subsided in surviving animals. Animals demonstrated decreasing levels of lymphocytes following a rapid spike post-challenge. Monocytes and eosinophils were slightly decreased with a trough at 24 hours post treatment. There was a “marked” increase in the basophil percentages in raxibacumab treated animals on day 5 post treatment.
L3030: The sponsor stated that the hematology data collected on this study suggested that the animals were demonstrating non-specific indicators of illness post-challenge.
L3031: **MO comment:** One animal in the placebo group had an initial WBC that was outside the normal range (low). That animal showed increasing WBCs until death. A number of animals had elevated WBCs during infection, independent of survival. The lowest platelet count while on study was 214 \times 10^3/\mu\text{L} in an animal in the 40 mg/kg raxibacumab group. The sponsor commented that there was a “marked” increase in basophil percentages in treated animals on day 5. The highest basophil percentage was 2.1% in an animal in the 40 mg/kg raxibacumab group. There were only 2 animals in the placebo group that had basophil levels drawn on day 5 and their percentages of basophils were 0.3% and 1.5%.
L3032: *The reviewer agrees with the sponsor's assessment that the hematology data are most suggestive of a non-specific process associated with the acute anthrax infection in these animals.*
L3033: ## Necropsy and Histopathology:
L3034: All animals found dead or euthanized had necropsies performed. In addition, all animals who did not survive had terminal blood cultures drawn and all animals that died had positive cultures for *B. anthracis*. Two monkeys did not have evidence of anthrax disease on gross examination. Histopathology was done on these two animals, and bacteria were noted (Table 13). Group 1 is raxibacumab 40 mg/kg and group 3 is placebo. Nephrosis and splenic lymphoid depletion were present in both monkeys. Large rod-shaped bacteria consistent with *B. anthracis* were present in multiple organs in both monkeys, particularly within the vasculature and in the splenic parenchyma. Lesions were more apparent in the control animal compared to the raxibacumab treated animal.

L3038: Tissue cultures of liver, spleen, and mediastinal lymph node were done for all animals that died. These tissue cultures were positive for all three tissues in 23 of the 24 animals. One animal had a negative lymph node culture but the other tissues were positive for bacteria.
L3039: **MO comment:** The animal that had a negative lymph node tissue culture was one of the animals that underwent histopathologic analysis. While the mediastinal lymph node was not positive, the brain, kidney, liver, spleen and lung were all positive for bacteria. Based on the information in the submission, it is suggested that the disease process might be slightly more intense in the control animal compared to the animal in the 40 mg/kg raxibacumab group. However, based on this preliminary information, it is not possible to evaluate differences between the two animals.

L3049: Of note, a number of animals had discoloration/foci/accumulation (red/dark) in the brain. It is interesting to note brain involvement in 3 of the 12 placebo animals, 6 of 7 animals in the 20 mg/kg raxibacumab group, and 3 of 5 animals in the 40 mg/kg raxibacumab group. There is a statistically significant difference between placebo and treated animals with respect to brain gross lesions, 3/12 in the placebo group compared to 9/12 in the treated groups (p=0.0391). Individual comparisons show significance for the placebo (3/12) compared to the 20 mg/kg raxibacumab group (6/7) (p=0.0198). No significance was seen for placebo (3/12) compared the 40 mg/kg raxibacumab group (3/5) (p=0.2801). These numbers are small but there is concern for the trend in placebo vs. treated animals. Based on this information, the sponsor was asked to perform histopathologic analysis on all tissues (with particular emphasis on the brains) for all animals that died during the study.
L3050: ## Protocol 901-G005829 and EPL Independent Pathology Assessment
L3051: The results of the histopathologic analysis of the tissues of all animals that died are presented in Table 16. All protocol-required tissues were evaluated with the exception of the mediastinal lymph node from animal C23036 which was not successfully processed to a slide. Microscopic findings were graded semi-quantitatively according to the scale:
L3052: - Grade 1 = minimal
- Grade 2 = mild
- Grade 3 = moderate
- Grade 4 = marked
L3053: Microscopic findings were considered consistent with anthrax disease in all animals that died. Animals treated with raxibacumab had a greater incidence and/or severity of CNS lesions than did placebo treated animals. "More
L3054: numerous and widespread bacteria were observed in the brain of Raxibacumab-treated animals, while bacteria in the brain of untreated control animals were often confined to blood vessels or the immediate perivascular space. However, untreated control animals had greater incidence and/or severity of parenchymal organ lesions did Raxibacumab-treated animals.” The conclusion by Battelle was that raxibacumab treated animals that died had a greater incidence of inflammation, hemorrhage, necrosis and bacteria in the brain. Further they argue that the median time to death for monkeys without inflammation was 3.2 days compared to 4.5 days in those that had inflammation. They also state that there was a significant improvement in survival time in treated animals based on the inclusion of time of survival data for animals that survive the challenge.
L3055: EPL also analyzed the histopathology slides and the summary of their data compared with the Battelle data is included in Table 17. For the most part, the findings were similar in both incidence and severity with a correlation coefficient of &gt; 0.85. EPL concluded, “By the EPL reading, the incidence of findings in the brain is not higher in the raxibacumab treatment groups compared with the placebo treatment groups, but the severity of the findings, particularly in the meninges, tends to be greater.”

L3112: ## EPL Analysis
L3113: The EPL findings were essentially similar to the Battelle findings. Of the 24 animals that were examined, there were differences between EPL and Battelle in 17 animals. However, the differences were primarily changes in one level of severity for single observations, ie. from minimal to mild. In looking at the overall severity of involvement for each of the animals (including observations of CNS bacteria, inflammation, hemorrhage, and necrosis), there was no difference between Battelle and EPL with respect to minimal involvement compared to significant CNS involvement. Neither analysis showed differences in the treated groups for presence of CNS bacteria. Both analyses showed significant differences in the treatment groups with respect to inflammation and hemorrhage. When any location of necrosis was considered, the EPL analysis showed a significant difference between the treatment groups with respect to necrosis, whereas the Battelle analysis did not show a difference.

L3122: No association between severity of CNS bacteria and length of survival or time of bacteremia was seen on either analysis. Severity of inflammation was associated with a longer time of survival in the Battelle analysis and a longer time of bacteremia before death in both Battelle and EPL analyses. The differences between Battelle and EPL hinge on one or two animals changing groups.
L3123: In looking at the presence compared to the absence of CNS bacteria, inflammation, hemorrhage and necrosis, both analyses demonstrated differences in time to survival and time of bacteremia for the presence of hemorrhage. There was no association between length of survival for CNS bacteria in either analysis. The Battelle analysis showed a correlation between length of survival and time of bacteremia for inflammation while the EPL analysis did not. The EPL analysis showed a correlation between length of survival and time of bacteremia with the presence of necrosis, while the Battelle analysis did not. The differences between Battelle and EPL hinge on one or two animals changing groups. Of note, there were only 2 levels of necrosis in the EPL analysis while there were 3 levels in the Battelle analysis.
L3124: For all the analyses, the findings, in general, were more pronounced in the raxibacumab 20mg/kg group than in the 40 mg/kg group. The sponsor concluded that the severity of the pathology could be correlated to time of survival. Table 32 lists the medians of survival for all the non-surviving animals by treatment group and based on the Battelle definition of low or high pathology (Table 30). Within the treatment groups, there appears to be a trend to longer survival, however, the numbers of low pathology animals in the raxibacumab treated groups are small, as are the number of high pathology animals in the placebo group.

L3128: ## STUDY 724-G005829 CONCLUSIONS
L3129: This was a parallel-group, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled GLP study in 40 healthy male and female cynomolgus monkeys to evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of a single IV dose of raxibacumab in anthrax spore inhalation-challenged monkeys experiencing symptoms of inhalation anthrax.
L3130: ## Efficacy conclusions:
L3131: - Raxibacumab at both 20 mg/kg and 40mg/kg given by IV bolus dose was superior to placebo in preventing inhalational anthrax induced mortality in bacteremic nonhuman primates (cynomolgus monkeys) (FDA primary efficacy analysis population) with a survival of 41.7% (p=0.0396) in the 20 mg/kg raxibacumab group and 69.2% (p=0.0016) in the 40 mg/kg raxibacumab group.
- In the intention to treat (ITT) efficacy analysis population (as treated challenged nonhuman primates regardless of bacteremia status) used by the sponsor, raxibacumab at 20 mg/kg demonstrated a 50% survival (p=0.0064) and raxibacumab at 40 mg/kg demonstrated a 64.3% survival (p=0.0007).
L3132: ## Safety conclusions:
L3133: - Safety data were limited in the study to findings on gross necropsy, histopathology, and serial CBCs.
- Gross brain lesions appeared to be more common in treated (9/12) compared to placebo (3/12) animals (p=0.0391). Two animals did not have
L3134: gross evidence of anthrax disease and histopathologic analysis was performed on those animals. Both animals had evidence of bacteria in the brain by histopathology. In these two animals, it was suggested that the disease was more prominent in the placebo treated animal compared to the raxibacumab treated animal.
L3135: - Based on the concern for an increase in the number of brain lesions in the treated animals, a complete histopathologic analysis was performed on all tissues from all animals that died. There were no significant differences in treated compared to control animals in the severity of pathologic lesions in any tissues other than the brain. In the brain, there were significant differences between treated and control animals in the incidence and severity of inflammation and hemorrhage in both the Battelle and the EPL analyses (of note, these were more pronounced in the raxibacumab 20 mg/kg group, and there did not seem to be a dose related effect although the numbers are small). While there was some correlation between severity of inflammation and hemorrhage with survival time and time of bacteremia to death in all animals when the groups were consolidated, the overall survival time and time from bacteremia to death based on treatment group would not seem to explain these differences. Based on the available analyses, the pathophysiologic basis for these differences is unclear. In addition, the number of animals analyzed is small and statistical differences hinge on single animals changing assigned groups. While it is reassuring that no gross neurologic findings were noted in the surviving animals (no formal testing was performed), and no brain abnormalities were seen in toxicologic studies, a potential interaction between anthrax and raxibacumab contributing to CNS inflammation and hemorrhage cannot be ruled out. It will be important to examine the histopathology in animals that die in any subsequent studies and it would be reassuring to examine the brains of those animals that survive in order to establish normal brain histology in survivors. If it is not possible to sacrifice survivors, then more formal neurologic assessments including imaging studies should be performed in subsequent studies.

L3150: Raxibacumab, also known as HGS1021, PA mAb, or ABthrax, is a recombinant, fully human IgG1λ mAb that binds *B. anthracis* PA with high affinity and inhibits its biological activity. Raxibacumab is expressed in the NS0 mouse myeloma cell line and secreted into culture media, from which it is purified by a series of chromatography and filtration steps.

L3158: **Background:** To date the Sponsor has conducted evaluation of raxibacumab in several animal species and under various conditions. Efficacy of raxibacumab was established in a proof-of concept rat model of Lethal Toxin infusion in pre-exposure and post-exposure setting. In addition, when used for pre-exposure prophylaxis raxibacumab showed dose-dependent survival benefit in rabbits and monkeys. Time-related effect on survival was also observed in post-exposure prophylaxis setting in a rabbit model.

L3176: At Regulatory Briefing on the applicability of the Animal Rule to the licensing of anthrax anti-toxin monoclonal antibodies held at CDER on October 10, 2006, a consensus was reached that the efficacy of the monoclonal antibody against anthrax toxin should be demonstrated in 2 animal species (rabbit and NHP). Both models must show a significant benefit of the monoclonal over placebo. In addition, both models should explore the magnitude of benefit of an antitoxin therapeutic when combined with an antimicrobial over antimicrobial alone.
L3177: This submission addresses the evaluation of raxibacumab efficacy over placebo in one of two proposed recommended animal models – rabbit.
L3178: The Sponsor provided the results inhalational anthrax natural history study in rabbit. The Sponsor claims the natural history of inhalational anthrax disease in the characterization studies in NZW rabbits conducted thus far demonstrated reproducible clear and predictable clinico-laboratory profile (body temperature, clinical hematology, PA toxemia, and bacteremia) that correlates with mortality (see following Table). In addition, it is claimed that correlation of PA toxemia and temperature elevation of \ge 2^\circ\text{F} to onset of bacteremia has been established in these studies.
L3179: **MO comment:** The Division has not yet reviewed the data from the natural history characterization study, but agrees that the completed efficacy study (the subject of this review), proved the above claimed correlations are true, could support the conclusions derived regarding raxibacumab efficacy in established inhalational anthrax.

L3196: **MO comment:** The treatment was administered as a bolus injection. In human studies raxibacumab is to be administered by 2.5 hour infusion. As we are trying to make a leap from animal to human efficacy, it is imperative to ensure that it will be possible to match animal and human PK parameters, i.e. Cmax and the duration of infusion may significantly impact the pharmacokinetics of the product.
L3197: - Clinical observations were collected bid after day 7
L3198: **MO comment:** Available information (sponsor's summary of the natural history of inhalational anthrax characterization study in rabbits, scientific literature on the subject, and presentations from veterinary laboratories conducting these studies) on the inhalational anthrax model in rabbits points to the very rapid progress of anthrax disease in rabbits (3-4 day survival post-challenge). Twice daily observations of the animals appear to be insufficient to determine the time of the animal's death if euthanasia was not performed. This will have a significant impact on time to death analyses in view of the fact that even 2-3 hours of additional survival time recorded might be crucial.
L3199: - Animals were euthanized if found moribund on D14
- Necropsy and histopathology were conducted on all euthanized and all dead animals
L3200: **MO comment:** It is important to confirm end-organ bacillary damage. Quantitative post mortem cultures of relevant organs were recommended to be provided. However, the Sponsor resorted only to identify bacteria in dead animals only on microscopic examination.
L3201: The FDA also asked for independent pathology review of the slides. The independent evaluation of the pathology slides was completed by Experimental Pathology Laboratories, Inc. (EPL). The draft report of their results was submitted as serial 0093 on December 23, 2008. At EPL, all the slides were read in a blinded manner and then peer reviewed.

L3206: ## Raxibacumab PK
L3207: PK analyses of raxibacumab concentration-time profiles for all raxibacumab-dosed rabbits were conducted using population analysis techniques with NONMEM software. Serum raxibacumab concentration-time data, serum PA concentration-time data, individual raxibacumab PK parameters, and individual PA kinetic parameters were summarized using descriptive statistics.

L3209: ## Endpoints:
L3210: **Primary efficacy endpoint** was survival in the ITT study population on Day 14
L3211: ## Analysis Populations:
L3212: - ITT population is defined as all randomized rabbits that received the study agent
- mITT population is defined as a subset of the ITT population that received raxibacumab or placebo (based on treatment group assigned, not actual treatment received)
- As randomized population defined as all rabbits that were randomized regardless of whether or not they were spore-challenged
- As treated population defined as the set of rabbits that received the study agent with the assignment to treatment group that was based on the actual treatment administered to the rabbits
L3213: **MO comment:** Because this pivotal study report will also be submitted for licensing application (BLA) for the treatment of inhalational anthrax in humans under the Animal Rule, it is important to ensure that the study population is sufficiently reflective of the human population with anthrax disease. Therefore, the Per Protocol population (all animals that were confirmed to have anthrax disease as evident by the presence of bacteremia at the time of treatment initiation) will be the study population the reviewer will be focusing efficacy assessments on. The outcomes in the ITT and mITT should trend in the same direction as the Per Protocol analysis.
L3214: ## Statistical Plan:
L3215: The sample size of 18 animals per study group provides 80% power at overall significance level of 0.05 to detect an absolute difference of 45% or more in 14 day survival in one of the raxibacumab treatment groups (20 or 40 mg/kg). Placebo survival is assumed to be 0 with 5% deviation. Raxibacumab survival is assumed to be 50%
L3216: The primary efficacy analysis will be performed using 2-sided likelihood ratio test or Fisher's exact test. Adjustment is made for multiple comparisons
L3217: **MO comment:** Please refer to the Statistical review by Zhou, Hongling, Ph. D.

L3243: ## Animal's Disposition
L3244: - *Animal L08147 was bacteremic by culture 1.4 hours prior to treatment with raxibacumab 40mg/kg; however, sample drawn immediately prior to raxibacumab administration did not grow bacteria. L3269: **MO comment:** The reviewer based her analyses below on the as treated population of animals: 16 in the placebo arm, 17 in the raxibacumab 20mg/kg, and 19 in the raxibacumab 40mg/kg arms. 55 to 76.4% of rabbits were febrile at or before the time of treatment initiation. The highest number of febrile rabbits (13/17, 76.4%) was observed in the 20mg/kg study group and the lowest (10/18, 55%) was in the 40mg/kg study group. 29/34(85.3%) of febrile animals (3 groups) were simultaneously toxemic and bacteremic before treatment initiation.
L3270: Toxemia was observed in approximately &gt;87% of all challenged rabbits at or before treatment initiation in each of the study groups. 43/46(93.5%) toxemic animals were bacteremic prior to treatment.
L3271: Bacteremia prior to treatment was documented by culture in greater than 89% of rabbits in both active treatment groups 20 and 40mg/kg and in 87.5% of placebo animals. 43/45 (95.6%) of bacteremic animals were also toxemic prior to treatment. Only positivity for
L3272: PA by ECL was not a good predictor of bacteremia. Only 32/45 (71.1%) of bacteremic animals were positive by ECL screen assay. And 30/45(66.7%) of bacteremic animals were febrile prior to treatment. However, PA screen in combination with temperature elevation was able to capture all animals bacteremic prior to treatment 45/45.
L3273: Median time to treatment administration as determined by the trigger (PA toxemia (ECL and or temperature rise) was longest for the 20mg/kg treatment group (28.1 hours) and shortest for the 40mg/kg (24.3hours). As the course of inhalational anthrax in rabbits is quite short; every hour from the time of diagnosis to treatment administration is critical.

L3296: ## **Other Parameters Measured:**
L3297: The majority of animals exhibited clinical signs consistent with anthrax following the spore challenge. The most common clinical features were lethargy, not eating, and respiratory abnormalities.
L3298: Body temperature was monitored in all animals. The readings were stable until approximately 30 hours post challenge, and then exhibited sharp increases above baseline, and
L3299: remained high until death among placebo-treated and raxibacumab-treated non-survivors. Among raxibacumab-treated survivors, body temperatures also increased around 30 hours post challenge, then gradually declined to and remained at baseline levels, with the exception of a second increase above baseline at approximately 80 hours post challenge from which they recovered by approximately 160 hours post challenge.
L3300: The *B. anthracis* MICs for levofloxacin, prior to treatment and the terminal MICs ranged from 0.5 to 4\mug/mL. For ciprofloxacin, the MICs prior to treatment ranged from 0.25 to 2\mug/mL, and the terminal MICs ranged from 0.125 to 2\mug/mL, demonstrating that the original MICs to these antibiotics did not change during the course of the study.
L3301: Body temperature was monitored in all animals.
L3302: No data on anti-PA antibody levels and TNA post-challenge were collected during the study.
L3303: All animals that survived were monitored for 14 days post-challenge. Clinical signs and symptoms of anthrax, including body temperature elevations, resolved following resolution of bacteremia. Animals exhibited normal baseline behavior at the time of study termination.
L3304: Animals found moribund were euthanized. All animals that died underwent pathological examination.
L3305: **MO comment:** Although the Division has recommended performing necropsy on all animals at the end of the study in communications with the Sponsor in the planning phase of the study, pathology data was collected only for the non-survivors, limiting reviewer's ability to perform analyses of the pathology findings that involved all animals that were treated with raxibacumab.

L3329: ## Efficacy conclusions:
L3330: - Raxibacumab at 40mg/kg IV bolus dose was superior to placebo in preventing inhalational anthrax induced mortality in bacteremic NZW rabbits (FDA primary efficacy analysis population) with achieved survival of 35% versus 0% (p=0.0237).
- Animal survival in raxibacumab 20mg/kg IV was not statistically different (p=0.1) from survival in the placebo group for the FDA primary efficacy analysis population of bacteremic NZW rabbits with achieved survival of 25% versus 0%.
- In the modified intention to treat efficacy analysis population (as treated challenged NZW rabbits regardless of bacteremia status) raxibacumab at both dosing regimens of 20mg/kg IV single bolus and 40mg/kg IV single bolus was superior to placebo in preventing inhalational anthrax induced mortality with achieved survival of 29.4% versus 0% (p=0.0445) and 42.1% (p=0.0038), respectively.
- In the intention to treat analysis (as randomized challenged NZW rabbits regardless of bacteremia status) raxibacumab at both dosing regimens of 20mg/kg IV single bolus and 40mg/kg IV single bolus was superior to placebo in preventing inhalational anthrax induced mortality with achieved survival of 27.8% versus 0% (p=0.0455) and 44.4% (p=0.0029), respectively.
- Additional exploratory analyses (as treated toxemic animals, all treated toxemic and bacteremic animals) revealed similar trend of improved survival in the raxibacumab treated animals without reaching statistical significance.

L3344: **MO comment:** Among rabbits that received raxibacumab, fewer organs contained visible bacteria than seen in placebo rabbits. It is important to note, however, that greater number of animals that succumbed to anthrax in either of the active treatment groups had brain pathology findings, including those consistent with meningitis (100% for raxibacumab 20mg/kg and 72.7% for raxibacumab 40mg/kg) as compared to placebo (25%). Also, greater number of animals in 40mg/kg raxibacumab group had pathologic changes in the heart as compared to placebo and 20mg/kg raxibacumab groups. Per calculations performed by statistical reviewer Hongling Zhou, Ph.D., the rates of rabbits with brain pathology were significantly different between the placebo group and the raxibacumab 20 mg/kg group (p = 0.0003, Fisher's exact test) even after the Bonferroni correction (0.05/2=0.025). The difference between the placebo group and the raxibacumab 40 mg/kg group was not significantly different (p = 0.0542, Fisher's exact test).
L3345: The study report states that the likely explanation for these findings is longer survival of the diseased animals in the active treatment groups as compared to placebo (in the 20 mg/kg raxibacumab group median = 3.5 days, and 40 mg/kg group median = 3.8 days, and in the placebo group median = 2.7 days). Also, the average time to death in rabbits with moderate inflammation in the brain was 4.5 days compared with 3.1 days in all rabbits that died, suggesting that the increased survival time allowed for additional pathology to develop in the brain. This finding is reported to be consistent with the reported observation that cynomolgus monkeys that survive longer post challenge have increased rates of meningeal hemorrhage and cerebral vasculitis (Vasconcelos et al, 2003).
L3346: **MO comment:** The Reviewer examined data and manipulations performed by the Sponsor that led to the above conclusion (submitted upon Reviewer's request) and determined that case ascertainment of moderate inflammation in the brain of the diseased animals was not consistent among individual animals, and, as disease progression in rabbits is very fast, rounding to a full day for the times to deaths is not acceptable.

L3369: **MO comment:** The Reviewer attempted to explore whether the treatment with raxibacumab might have caused accelerated bacterial translocation into meninges (shorter duration of bacteremia prior to treatment) and, therefore, brain pathology (the first 3 analyses). In fact, raxibacumab treated animals that developed meningitis had slightly longer duration of bacteremia prior to treatment as compared to those without meningitis. On the other hand, additional analyses of bacteremia duration prior to death seem to support the Sponsor's claim for the longer duration of illness (in this case duration of bacteremia) almost 2.5-3 fold prior to death for animals with CNS findings, including bacteria, as compared to those animals that died without CNS involvement. Additional analyses were performed to explore the correlation between the duration of bacteremia and severity of CNS inflammation. A trend towards numerically longer duration of bacteremia prior to death was observed in animals with moderate/severe inflammation as compared to those with minimal/mild CNS inflammatory changes. Also, raxibacumab treated animals that succumbed to anthrax had numerically longer mean and median duration of bacteremia prior to death as compared to placebo treated animals. Unexplained, however, remains the finding of longer time to bacteremia after the spore challenge in the placebo animals that died as compared to raxibacumab treated animals. Sampling bias should not have occurred as blood samples for culture were collected per protocol every 4 hours starting 12 hours post-challenge in all animals regardless of the group assignment.
L3370: ## Safety conclusions:
L3371: - Raxibacumab at 40mg/kg IV offered a statistically significant survival benefit to the NZW rabbits with established systemic inhalational anthrax disease evident by bacteremia prior to therapeutic intervention.
- Frequent and more extensive findings of CNS pathology in raxibacumab treated animals on necropsy as compared to placebo are possibly associated with a longer
L3372: duration of illness, i.e. documented bacteremia by culture, prior to death in the raxibacumab treated animals. However, monoclonal-disease interaction could not be excluded. This pathology finding should be described in the resultant label of raxibacumab if approved, especially if corroborated by the similar findings in NHP anthrax treatment study.

L3393: **To:** Edward Cox, MD, MPH

**BLA:** 125349

**Submission Date:** 5/14/09

**Date Review Completed:** 5/29/09

**Product:** Raxibacumab (monoclonal antibody against Protective Antigen of *B. anthracis*)

**Sponsor:** Human Genome Sciences, Inc.
Rockville, MD

**Proposed Indication:** Treatment of anthrax

**Proposed Dosing Regimen:** A single intravenous infusion of 40 mg/kg dose
L3394: A Biologics Licensing Application (BLA) under 21 CFR 601, Subpart H. for raxibacumab, a fully human monoclonal antibody against Protective antigen of *B. anthracis*, for the treatment of anthrax was submitted on 13 May 2009. This submission contained a request for a Priority Review. However, the Sponsor did not provide written justification for such a request. In response to the Division's letter dated May 21, 2009, HGS provided additional information justifying their request that the raxibacumab BLA be considered for Priority Review, as discussed below.
L3395: Under BB-IND 11,069 initiated in June 2003 raxibacumab was assigned Fast Track status and was granted Orphan Drug designation (03-17550) for the treatment of anthrax on 15 August 2003 and 12 November 2003, respectively. Both Fast Track status and Orphan Drug designation carry the requirement that the drug addresses an unmet medical need (Guidance for Industry Fast Track Drug Development Programs - Designation, Development, and Application Review [January 2006] and 21 CFR 316.20, respectively).
L3396: **MO comment:** Anthrax disease is associated with 3 known virulence factors of *B. anthracis*: antiphagocytic capsule and two protein exotoxins: lethal and edema toxins. As in most infections
L3397: antibacterial treatment will result in killing and eradication of the susceptible bacteria. However, in case of anthrax antimicrobials alone are not sufficient to abort the part of the disease pathogenesis that is triggered by the toxins. A crucial component of *B. anthracis* toxins is PA (protective antigen) that results in a heptamer formation on the target cell membrane and allows entry of the lethal and edema factors intracellularly to exert their cytopathic effect. Raxibacumab has a novel mechanism of action distinct from the action of antimicrobials; by binding with high affinity to PA of *B. anthracis* it prevents formation of active toxins and diminishes their downstream pathologic effects.
L3398: HGS requested consideration for Priority Review for the raxibacumab BLA application for therapeutic treatment of inhalation anthrax as the application satisfies the criteria for Priority Review outlined in CDER MAPP 6020.3 on Priority and Standard Review, that is, raxibacumab provides safe and effective therapy where no satisfactory alternative therapy exists and provides significant improvement compared to marketed products in treating anthrax disease.
L3399: **Demonstration of effectiveness:** Raxibacumab provided a statistically significant improvement in survival rate as compared to placebo in pivotal efficacy studies in 2 different species when raxibacumab was administered to the animals with confirmed inhalational anthrax disease. The demonstration of efficacy in 2 animal species is consistent with the requirements outlined in the Animal Rule (21CFR 601 Subpart H).
L3400: **MO comment:** The evidence of efficacy of raxibacumab as a single 40mg/kg IV dose as compared to placebo in a setting of established inhalational anthrax disease in two animal models (NZW rabbits and cynomolgus monkeys) was reviewed previously for the raxibacumab acquisition by Strategic National Stockpile. The reviewers concurred with the Sponsor's conclusions that administration of raxibacumab in this setting in both animal species resulted in statistically significant survival benefit as compared to placebo. The Sponsor collected and provided sufficient information to conclude that the requirements for demonstration of efficacy of raxibacumab under the Animal Rule (21CFR 601, Subpart H) are met.
L3401: **Demonstration that no satisfactory alternative therapy exists and that raxibacumab provides a significant improvement compared to marketed products in treating anthrax disease:** Raxibacumab is a fully human monoclonal antibody against the PA of *Bacillus anthracis*. It has a novel mechanism of action of binding and inhibiting the action of bacterial toxin as compared with the currently marketed products that act by virtue of their bactericidal or bacteriostatic activity (see prescribing information for CIPRO, Levaquin and Vibramycin). While vaccine containing PA has been licensed to promote the generation of antibodies to PA, vaccines do not provide immediate anti-toxin activity and require weeks and multiple injections to provide significant protection (see prescribing information for AVA [Biothrax]). There is no satisfactory alternative therapy which provides immediate anti-toxin (anti-PA) activity leading to a survival benefit. Moreover, the effectiveness of raxibacumab in improving survival has been demonstrated in the setting of therapeutic treatment when animals have documented anthrax disease, in contrast to the currently marketed products in where their effectiveness in treating anthrax was derived from either *in vitro* activity data or from the studies in animals in the setting of post-exposure prophylaxis (see prescribing information for CIPRO, Levaquin and Vibramycin, and Friedlander et al, 1993) and anthrax vaccine (Friedlander et al, 1993) or in
L3402: humans in the setting of post-exposure prophylaxis with ciprofloxacin following the anthrax attacks of 2001 (see CIPRO prescribing information) or in the setting of pre-exposure prophylaxis with vaccine (see Biothrax prescribing information). In addition, raxibacumab provides an alternative therapy when antibiotics or vaccines are contraindicated (see contraindications and warnings in the prescribing information for CIPRO, Levaquin, Vibramycin and Biothrax), and for subjects who are non-compliant. Furthermore, in the event of an anthrax disease due antibiotic-resistant bacteria, which can be bioengineered (Anthamna et al, 2004), raxibacumab might be the only therapy to provide immediate effective treatment.
L3403: **MO comment:** As discussed previously the novel mechanism of action allows raxibacumab to be used for treatment of inhalational anthrax not only in combination with antibiotics as it is anticipated, but also in the settings where antimicrobials are poorly tolerated, contraindicated, or are ineffective due to resistance.
L3404: **Demonstration of safety:** Raxibacumab was evaluated in over 400 subjects, of whom over 300 received raxibacumab at the to-be-marketed dose and route of administration. Raxibacumab was safe, well tolerated, and non-immunogenic when administered as single or repeat dose. The incidence of all adverse events (AEs), related AEs, severe AEs and serious AEs (SAE) was in raxibacumab-treated subjects was comparable to subjects who received placebo. SAEs were rare with only a single SAE (cholecystitis) reported as possibly related to raxibacumab, although the investigator judged the event to be most likely related to the subject's pre-existing, underlying medical condition. Concomitant administration of raxibacumab with antibiotics in healthy humans did not alter the safety or pharmacokinetics (PK) of either antibiotic or raxibacumab and in animals did not alter antibiotic efficacy or PK.
L3405: **MO comment:** Safety data limited to 82 healthy subjects that received single 40mg/kg IV dose of raxibacumab alone and in combination with ciprofloxacin were reviewed prior to the product acquisition by the SNS. The reviewers concurred with the Sponsor that the use of product was associated with mild histamine mediated infusion reactions and now requires diphenhydramine premedication. Otherwise, its safety profile was comparable to that of placebo. The BLA application contains additional safety data &gt;200 additional healthy subjects, that brings the total safety database for this product to over 300.
L3406: **Conclusion:** Based on the evidence provided above, the Reviewer agrees with the Sponsor's proposal that raxibacumab satisfies the criteria for Priority Review because raxibacumab provides safe and effective therapy where no satisfactory alternative therapy exists and provides a significant improvement compared to marketed products in treating anthrax disease.

L3418: PA: A Potential Therapeutic Target
Diagram illustrating the mechanism of action of Raxibacumab. The diagram shows the anthrax toxin components: PA20, PA63, LF (Lethal Factor), and EF (Edema Factor). Raxibacumab targets the PA20 component, preventing the formation of the ATR (or CMG2) complex. The ATR complex is necessary for the translocation of LF and EF into the host cell. LF inhibits MAPKs (MEKs), leading to Disrupted Signal Transduction. EF inhibits cAMP, leading to Edema. The diagram also defines LT = PA + LF and ET = PA + EF.
FDA

The Survivor line shows a rise in PA levels starting around day 3, peaking around day 7 (near 100 ng/mL), and then declining rapidly, stabilizing near 1 ng/mL by day 9.

L3448: Figure: Survival Curves for Cynomolgus Monkeys. The graph plots Survival Probability (Y-axis, 0.0 to 1.0) against Time (days) (X-axis, 0 to 25). Four groups are compared: Diluent (Control), 10 mg/kg, 20 mg/kg, and 40 mg/kg. The Diluent group shows 0% survival by day 5. The 40 mg/kg group shows 90% survival by day 28. The 20 mg/kg group shows 70% survival by day 28. The 10 mg/kg group shows 60% survival by day 28. Statistical significance is indicated: p = 0.0001 for the difference between Diluent and 40 mg/kg, and p = 0.0005 for the difference between Diluent and 20 mg/kg, and Diluent and 10 mg/kg.

L3453: Kaplan-Meier survival curve showing survival probability versus time (days) for three treatment groups: Placebo, 20 mg/kg, and 40 mg/kg. The Placebo group shows the lowest survival probability, followed by the 20 mg/kg group, and the 40 mg/kg group shows the highest survival probability, with many animals surviving beyond 28 days. Statistical results are noted: Log-Rank test for overall treatment effect p value = 0.0003; p = 0.0004 (vs. Placebo) for the 20 mg/kg group; p = 0.0029 (vs. Placebo) for the 40 mg/kg group. HGS# 000-6727.
L3454: Kaplan-Meier Survival Curves for FDA Primary Analysis.
The graph plots Survival Probability (Y-axis, 0.0 to 1.0) against Survival Time in Days (X-axis, 0 to 25). Three treatment groups are compared:
Placebo (Solid line)
Raxibacumab 20 mg/kg (Dashed line)
Raxibacumab 40 mg/kg (Dotted line)
The Placebo group shows the lowest survival probability, dropping significantly around day 5. The Raxibacumab 20 mg/kg group shows intermediate survival, dropping around day 10. The Raxibacumab 40 mg/kg group shows the highest survival probability, remaining near 1.0 until approximately day 15, after which it drops to about 0.7.

L3457: Figure 4: Survival curve showing dose-response survival of Fisher 344 rats challenged with lethal toxin, administered antibody at t = -2 to -8 weeks. Survival decreases as the time of antibody administration increases, with 100% survival observed for PAmAb587 10x at t = -2, -3 wk.
L3458: Graph showing % Survival versus Days post-challenge for Rabbit Anthrax Inhalational Model. The Y-axis is % Survival (0 to 100) and the X-axis is Days post-challenge (0 to 14). The Vehicle group shows 0% survival by Day 3. Dose groups (5 mg/kg, 10 mg/kg, 20 mg/kg, 40 mg/kg) show increasing survival rates, with 20 mg/kg and 40 mg/kg groups achieving approximately 50% survival by Day 14. The 20 mg/kg group administered 36 hours post-challenge shows slightly lower survival compared to the 20 mg/kg group administered 24 hours post-challenge.
L3459: Figure 6: Survival curves for pre-exposure prophylaxis in monkeys. The graph shows survival probability versus time (days). Four groups are compared: Diluent, 10 mg/kg, 20 mg/kg, and 40 mg/kg. The survival probability decreases over time for all groups. The 10 mg/kg group shows the highest survival probability, followed by 20 mg/kg, and then 40 mg/kg. The Diluent group shows the lowest survival probability. Statistical significance (p-values) are indicated for comparisons between the Diluent group and the other three groups: p = 0.0001 for 10 mg/kg, p = 0.0005 for 20 mg/kg, and p = 0.0005 for 40 mg/kg.
